title: Unified hook drain: frame-0 hooks stop firing after the first loop; a phase-carried cycle swap or a reverse-to-forward flip fires every early hook at once
decomp_evidence: CSequence::update_internal (acclient.c:340659). The forward loop `for (...; _floor(*_frame_number) > (double)v6; ++v6) ... CSequence::execute_hooks(v22, part_frame(v6), 1)` (340713-340726) fires each frame crossed in this quantum exactly once. At a cycle wrap, advance_to_next_animation sets `*_curr_anim = v24->first_cyclic; *_frame_number = get_starting_frame(...)` (340566-340567) and the loop resumes with `quantum = time_left` (340776), so frame low's hooks fire again on every pass. Nothing fires for frames the playhead did not cross in this update.
openac_evidence: OpenAC CSequence.cs:216-302 UpdateInternal fires ExecuteHooks(GetPartFrame(lastFrame), +1) (line 254) only for frames crossed in the current call. Test CSequenceUpdateTests.cs:112 Forward_CyclicWrap_NoAnimDone_RestartsAtStartingFrame: the wrap lands on frame 0 so it fires on the next pass. Holtburger's own retired planner scene3d/hook_windows.js:49-55 already uses `[-Infinity, currentTime]` as the second window of a wrap.
holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js:9412-9422 `_drainUnifiedHooks`: on a wrap, `ua.lastHookTime = 0;` (9418), then `_fireHooksInRange(.., ua.lastHookTime, curT)`, whose filter `if (t <= lowExclusive) continue;` (15712) skips every hook at t=0 from then on. Burst 1: `_installUnifiedLoco` calls `seq.seekPhase(prev.seq.phase)` (9239) on a record created with `lastHookTime: -1` (9249), so the first drain fires (-1, curT], i.e. every hook between frame 0 and the carried phase at once. Burst 2: the reverse branch sets `lo.lastHookTime = -1; // no reverse footfall spam` (15152). setMotion dedups the same cacheKey (10711-10718) and backstep reuses WalkForward's key, so when the player steps forward again the same record fires the same (-1, curT] burst.
discrepancy: Retail fires each crossed frame's hooks once per loop, frame low included, and never fires hooks the playhead did not cross. In holtburger, (a) every cycle's frame-0 hooks fire on the first loop only; (b) a walk-to-run swap with no link, and any reverse-to-forward flip, fires all hooks from frame 0 up to the current phase in one tick (stacked footstep sounds and particles).
proposed_change: In `_drainUnifiedHooks` (entities.js:9404-9424), on a wrap set the cursor to -Infinity, not 0, before the head window. Better, compute the windows with the tested pure `planHookWindows` (scene3d/hook_windows.js, isRunning=!seq.done, isLoopOnce=!cyclic). In `_installUnifiedLoco`, after seekPhase, seed `lastHookTime` with the carried frame's time (`d.frameTimes[seq.globalFrameIndex]`) so the first drain fires only frames crossed after the swap. In the reverse branch (15141-15153), set `lo.lastHookTime` to the new position's frame time instead of -1. csequence-3 replaces this branch for good.
test_plan: Extend test_hook_windows.mjs with two cases. (1) Second-loop wrap: lastTime 0.3 → currentTime 0.05, dur 0.4, cyclic. Assert the windows cover t=0 (head window starts at -Infinity). (2) Seeded cursor: lastTime == currentTime == carried frame time. Assert no window fires anything. Run `node test_hook_windows.mjs`. If the drain moves into a pure helper, add a new `node test_unified_hook_drain.mjs` with a stub seq covering wrap, phase-carry install and reverse→forward resume.
already_tracked: no. A5-sequence-playback.md (2026-06-11) #3/#4 covered the mixer-era drain; planHookWindows went dead when the mixer was deleted (8f8141ca), and the live drain lost its -Infinity wrap.

verify.reasons:
Decomp: CSequence::update_internal (acclient.c:340659). The forward loop `for (...; _floor(*_frame_number) > (double)v6; ++v6) {... execute_hooks(get_part_frame(v6), 1)}` fires each crossed frame once per update. A wrap goes through advance_to_next_animation (`*_curr_anim = v24->first_cyclic; *_frame_number = get_starting_frame(...)`) and continues with `quantum = time_left`, so frame low fires again on every loop.

Holtburger (all re-read):
(a) entities.js:9412-9419. On a wrap the drain fires (last, dur] and then sets `ua.lastHookTime = 0;` (9418). `_fireHooksInRange` skips `if (t <= lowExclusive) continue;` (15712). So t=0 hooks fire on the first pass (cursor -1) and never again.

verify.implementation_notes:
Files: scene3d/hook_windows.js (new pure exports), scene3d/entities.js, test_hook_windows.mjs, docs/url-flags.md.

1. Add `export function unifiedHookTime(gf, frameTimes, framerate)` to hook_windows.js. It returns `(frameTimes && gf < frameTimes.length) ? frameTimes[gf] : (framerate > 0 ? gf / framerate : 0)`, which is exactly the curT formula at entities.js:9408-9411.
2. Add `export function planUnifiedHookDrain(lastHookTime, curT, dur)`. It returns `{ windows: Array<[lo, hi]>, cursor }`:
   - curT < last (wrap): windows `[[last, dur]]` (only if dur > last), plus `[-1, curT]` if curT > -1. Cursor = curT.
   - curT > last: `[[last, curT]]`, cursor = curT.
   - else: no windows, cursor unchanged.
3. In `_drainUnifiedHooks` (9404-9424), replace the body after the hooks check with the planner, then loop the windows through `_fireHooksInRange`.
4. In `_installUnifiedLoco` (9227-9256), set `let seedT = -1`. When the seekPhase carry ran (carryPhase && !hold && prev?.seq && !prev.hold), set `seedT = unifiedHookTime(seq.globalFrameIndex, d.frameTimes, +d.framerate || 0)` and use `lastHookTime: seedT` in the record. The carried frame's own hooks are skipped; they were entered by teleport.
5. In the reverse branch (15140-15153), replace `lo.lastHookTime = -1` with `lo.lastHookTime = unifiedHookTime(lo.seq.globalFrameIndex, lo.desc.frameTimes, +lo.desc.framerate || 0)`.
6. Escape flag `?unifiedHookCursor`. Default-ON reader: `?.toLowerCase() !== "off"`. `=off` restores the old reset-to-0 and -1 seeding. Add a url-flags.md row in the hookDrain/signedMotionSpeed table format.

Tests (`node test_hook_windows.mjs`):
(i) Second-loop wrap: last 0.3, curT 0.0, dur 0.4. Expect windows [[0.3,0.4],[-1,0]], so the hook at t=0 is included.
(ii) Wrap landing past frame 0: last 0.3, curT 0.1. Expect windows [[0.3,0.4],[-1,0.1]].
(iii) Seeded cursor equal to curT: no windows.
(iv) unifiedHookTime with frameTimes and with the framerate fallback.
Also assert in a tiny table that a hook at t=0 passes the (lo, hi] filter for lo=-1.

title: Hooks fire when a frame is entered and on each node's last frame; retail fires a frame's hooks when the playhead leaves it and never fires the last (high_frame) frame. Emit hook events from the Rust playhead.
decomp_evidence: update_internal, forward branch (acclient.c:340700-340726): `if (get_high_frame < floor(fn)) { time_left = (fn - high - 1)/framerate; advance_anim = 1; *_frame_number = (double)high_frame; }` then `for (; _floor(*_frame_number) > (double)v6; ++v6) { combine pos_frame(v6); apply_physics(1/framerate); execute_hooks(get_part_frame(v6), 1); }`. v6 starts at the old floor, so hooks fire for the frame being LEFT, and after the clamp the loop stops at high-1: high_frame's hooks never fire. get_high_frame reads AnimSequenceNode+0x18 = high_frame (acclient.h:31063-31069). The reverse branch (340733-340759) mirrors this with low_frame never firing. anim_done_hook is queued after the crossed-frame hooks when head != first_cyclic (340764-340773).
openac_evidence: OpenAC CSequence.cs:234-254 matches the decomp (clamp `FrameNumber = currAnim.HighFrame` at 241; ExecuteHooks(lastFrame, +1) at 254; AddAnimDoneHook at 298). Tests: CSequenceUpdateTests.cs:88 Forward_SingleTick_AdvancesOneFrame_FiresExitedFrameHook (tick 0→1 fires f0); :126-139 Forward_LinkToCycle_FiresAnimDone_AndCarriesLeftover, where a 2-frame link yields events [link0, ANIMDONE, cyc0] and link1 never fires. ACE Sequence.update_internal has the same shape.
holt_evidence: src/lib.rs:24424-24430 stamps every hook with `time_in_clip_s: frame_time` (the frame's start time); animation.js:810 `time: +h.timeInClipS`. entities.js:9408-9422 fires (lastHookTime, ft[gf]], where gf is the displayed frame, so a frame's hooks fire as soon as it is drawn: frame 0 at play start, and the clamped last frame when a one-shot completes (time clamped to duration, motion_sequence.rs:286-290). Completion fires one record-level animationsDone(q, numAnims) (entities.js:15120-15127 → `_unifiedOneShotFinished`), with no per-node AnimDone.
discrepancy: Every animation hook (sounds, particles, SetOmega, Ethereal and others) fires one frame early: 33 ms at 30 fps, 67 ms at 15 fps. Hooks authored on a node's last frame (each AnimData segment of windup/strike/recover, link ends) fire in holtburger but never in retail. AnimDone is per record, not per completed link node.
proposed_change: In src/motion_sequence.rs, have advance_impl record crossed-frame events. Within a node, push `frame_offset + f` for every local frame LEFT (f_before .. f_after-1). When a node completes, push f_before .. num_frames-2, leaving out the last frame as retail's clamp does. Then push an ANIM_DONE sentinel (u32::MAX) if the completed node is non-cyclic. Expose an `eventCount` getter and `takeEvents()` (Vec<u32>, read only when count > 0 to avoid per-tick allocation). Clear events in reset_impl and in seek_phase_impl, since seeking must not fire hooks. Add `frame_index: u32` to HookDataPlain (lib.rs ~24426) and the JS hook snapshot (animation.js ~810), and build a per-descriptor frame→hooks index once. Replace the time-window drain in `_drainUnifiedHooks` with: for each event, fire that frame's hooks; for ANIM_DONE, call animationsDone(q, 1) per node instead of numAnims at the end.
test_plan: New #[test]s in the motion_sequence.rs tests module. `hooks_fire_on_frame_exit`: 4 frames @10fps, advance 0.1 → events [0], displayed frame 1. `terminal_frame_never_reported`: a 2-frame non-cyclic link chained to a 4-frame cycle (chain_impl), advance 0.3 → events [0, ANIM_DONE, 2], mirroring OpenAC Forward_LinkToCycle. `seek_does_not_emit`. The orchestrator then runs `cargo test -p holtburger-web --lib motion_sequence` (capped) and `node test_motion_sequence_wasm_smoke.mjs` after the wasm rebuild.

verify.reasons:
Decomp re-read: update_internal forward branch, acclient.c:340696-340731.
- `if ((double)get_high_frame(...) < floor(i)) { ...; *_frame_number = (double)get_high_frame(...); advance_anim = 1; }` and then `for (; _floor(*_frame_number) > (double)v6; ++v6) execute_hooks(get_part_frame(v6), 1)`.
- v6 starts at the OLD floor, so the hooks fired belong to the frame being LEFT.
- After the clamp the loop stops at high-1, so high_frame's hooks never fire. This holds even for a cyclic node at its wrap.
- get_high_frame is ICF-aliased as `AnimSequenceNode::get_high_frame(ChatRoomTracker*)`, which returns mOlthoiChatRoomID at offset 0x18. AnimSequenceNode = PackObj vtbl(0) + DLListData(4,8) + anim(0xC) + framerate(0x10) + low_frame(0x14) + high_frame(0x18) (acclient.h:31063-31069). So the alias reads high_frame.
- PhysicsDesc::get_animframe_id returns mRoleplayChatRoomID at 0x14 = low_frame (the reverse clamp).
- anim_done_hook is queued after the crossed-frame hooks when head != first_cyclic (LABEL_33 block).

OpenAC CSequence.cs:216-302 matches the decomp. Its tests agree: CSequenceUpdateTests.cs:88 (tick 0 to 1 fires f0), :99 Forward_ExactBoundaryLanding (3.5 to 4.0 fires only f3), and :126 Forward_LinkToCycle (events link0, ANIMDONE, cyc0; link1 never fires). ACE Sequence.cs:366/389 has the same shape.

Holtburger: hooks are stamped with the frame start time (lib.rs:24424-24430; animation.js:810 `time: +h.timeInClipS`). The drain fires (lastHookTime, ft[gf]] where gf is the DISPLAYED frame (entities.js:9408-9422), so frame f fires when it is entered, one anim frame earlier than retail. A completed one-shot clamps to its last frame (`self.time = self.nodes[self.node_index].duration`, motion_sequence.rs:287-289), so the last frame's hooks fire, and segment-last frames fire inside multi-AnimData links.

A5-sequence-playback.md row #3 describes retail as firing trailing hooks in (lastHookTime, duration], which wrongly includes the last frame. Not in PARITY-STATUS.
verify.corrections:
The proposed fix is over-scoped. It needs no Rust event channel, no wasm rebuild and no per-node AnimDone.

1. JS-only works. In the bake, frame_times are strictly increasing (dt > 0, and holds use 1/30). A hook's time is the f64 widening of the same f32 frame time that JS holds in desc.frameTimes (Float32Array), so time maps to frame exactly. Retail's rule then becomes: fire hooks with lo <= t < hi (inclusive low, exclusive high, where hi = the displayed frame's start time), and never fire a hook stamped on a segment's LAST frame.
2. Reverse-baked segments come out right automatically. The bake reverses frame order and negates direction (lib.rs build_concatenated_motion_frames reverse arm). Baked frame 0 is orig high, which retail fires when the playhead leaves it going down. The baked last frame is orig low, which retail never fires.
3. Do NOT change the J5 queue to per-node animationsDone. Record-level animationsDone(q, numAnims) is the deliberate J5 design (entities.js:9305-9310), and splitting it changes queue promotion timing for no hook-parity gain.
4. The Rust takeEvents/frame_index design can come later if multi-loop-per-tick precision is ever needed.
verify.implementation_notes:
Implement AFTER csequence-1, on its planUnifiedHookDrain helper.

1. In hook_windows.js, add `export function segmentLastTimes(desc)`. It returns a Set of `desc.frameTimes[s + c - 1]` for each (s, c) in segmentStarts/segmentCounts. With no segments it uses the single frame `numFrames - 1`, and falls back to `gf / framerate` when frameTimes is absent. Cache it on the record (`rec._segLast`) or on the descriptor.
2. Add `export function hookFiresOnExit(t, lo, hi, segLast)`, which is `t >= lo && t < hi && !segLast.has(t)`.
3. In planUnifiedHookDrain, under the flag, emit half-open windows:
   - wrap: `[last, dur)` then `[-1, curT)`.
   - monotonic: `[last, curT)`.
   A fresh record (cursor -1) at curT 0 fires nothing; frame 0 fires once the display reaches frame 1. A completing one-shot sits at curT = ft[n-1], so the last frame is excluded automatically.
4. Add `_fireHooksInRangeExit(inst, timeline, lo, hi, segLast, ...)` next to `_fireHooksInRange` (15705). It is the same loop with the half-open test and segLast skip, and the same HOOK_DRAIN_ON queue push.
5. Leave the phase-carry seed and the reverse-branch seed (= current frame time) unchanged. Under exit semantics the carried frame fires when the playhead leaves it.
6. Escape flag `?hookFrameExit`. Default-ON (`!== "off"`); `=off` restores the (lo, hi] filter with no exclusion. Add a url-flags.md row citing acclient.c:340700-340726.

Tests (`node test_hook_windows.mjs`):
(i) 4 frames at 10 fps, one hook per frame (t = 0, .1, .2, .3), segLast {0.3}.
   - cursor -1 to curT 0: nothing.
   - curT 0.1: f0.
   - 0.1 to 0.3: f1, f2.
   - wrap 0.3 to 0.1: f3 excluded, then f0.
(ii) Two-segment link (segments [0,2] counts [2,2], frameTimes [0,.1,.2,.3], dur .4), played to completion: fires f0 and f2 only. This mirrors OpenAC Forward_LinkToCycle, where link1 never fires.
(iii) A single-frame segment never fires.

title: Reverse playback (backstep, left strafe, left turn) is a per-tick JS seekPhase with all hooks suppressed; retail runs negative-framerate nodes through update_internal's reverse branch and fires Both and Backward hooks
decomp_evidence: Negative speed reaches the node framerate: AnimData*speed, and AnimSequenceNode::multiply_framerate (340968-340979) swaps low/high when the multiplier is negative. CSequence::multiply_cyclic_animation_fr (339736-339742) re-rates the cyclic nodes in place without touching frame_number. get_starting_frame returns `high_frame + 1 - 0.00019999999` for framerate < 0 (341016-341025). In the frame_quantum < 0 branch (340733-340759), frame_number decreases, crossed frames go through `execute_hooks(get_part_frame(v6), -1)`, and execute_hooks fires `if (!v5 || dir == v5)` (339695), i.e. Both and Backward. At low_frame, advance_to_next_animation with quantum >= 0 moves to next or first_cyclic at get_starting_frame (340563-340567): the list is still walked forward and each node plays backward.
openac_evidence: OpenAC CSequence.cs:264-282 (reverse branch, ExecuteHooks(.., -1) at 280); AnimSequenceNode.cs:55-62 MultiplyFramerate swaps low/high; test CSequenceUpdateTests.cs:147-157 Reverse_DescendingHooks_BackwardDirection (hooks f4 then f3 fire). Two OpenAC deviations not to copy: AnimSequenceNode.cs:51 GetStartingFrame returns the integer HighFrame+1 without retail's -0.0002, so the first reverse tick reads an out-of-range frame; and AnimationSequencer BuildBlendedFrame lerps/slerps, whereas retail CPartArray::UpdateParts (acclient.c:326601) is discrete.
holt_evidence: motion_sequence.rs:225-231: advance_impl runs `while remaining > 0.0`, so a negative dt does nothing. entities.js:15140-15153: on a negative step, `let p = lo.seq.phase + step / dur; p -= Math.floor(p); lo.seq.seekPhase(p);` then `lo.lastHookTime = -1; // no reverse footfall spam`. SIGNED_MOTION_SPEED is default-on (entities.js:1360-1363). seek_phase_impl (motion_sequence.rs:340-346) resets and re-advances from t=0 every frame. `_fireHook` always drops `direction === -1` (entities.js:15767).
discrepancy: While backstepping, strafing left or turning left (WalkForward/SideStepRight/TurnRight at negative speed), holtburger fires no animation hooks; retail fires the Both and Backward hooks, so footstep and SoundTable hooks go silent. Seeking a whole concatenated list backward also plays the nodes of a multi-node sequence in reverse order; retail walks the list forward and plays each node backward.
proposed_change: Give MotionNode a signed `rate` (default +1.0) and add `multiply_cyclic_framerate(m)` (wasm `multiplyCyclicFramerate`) that scales `rate` for nodes from first_cyclic_index onward, as multiply_cyclic_animation_fr does. In advance_impl, move each node's local time by dt*rate. A node with rate < 0 starts at time = duration - eps (retail's high+1-eps start) and completes when time < 0, carrying the spill forward. The list is still walked forward (next, or first_cyclic). Report frames left in descending order with dir -1, leaving out frame 0 (the last frame in reverse), using csequence-2's event channel (e.g. a direction bit). In JS: call `lo.seq.multiplyCyclicFramerate(-1)` once when `_motionSpeedSign` flips, always advance by |step|, delete the seekPhase branch (15140-15153), and change `_fireHook` to take dir and gate `direction === 0 || direction === dir` instead of the fixed `=== -1` drop. Reverse segments the bake already negated stay correct: the bake negation times the runtime reversal gives the original direction.
test_plan: New #[test] in the motion_sequence.rs tests module: `negative_rate_cycle_plays_backward_reports_dir_minus1`. 4 frames @10fps cyclic; multiply_cyclic_framerate(-1); the start displays frame 3; advance 0.1 → displays frame 2 with event (3, dir -1); advancing past frame 0 wraps back to frame 3 without reporting frame 0. Mirrors OpenAC Reverse_DescendingHooks_BackwardDirection. Also `multi_node_reverse_keeps_forward_list_order`. After the orchestrator's rebuild, extend `node test_motion_sequence_wasm_smoke.mjs` with a multiplyCyclicFramerate(-1) case.

verify.reasons:
The divergence is real.
- Holtburger: motion_sequence.rs:225-231 `while remaining > 0.0` ignores negative dt. The JS reverse branch (entities.js:15140-15153) computes `p = lo.seq.phase + step / dur; p -= Math.floor(p); lo.seq.seekPhase(p)` and sets `lo.lastHookTime = -1` without calling `_drainUnifiedHooks`, so no hook fires during a backstep, a left strafe or a left turn. The commands are rewritten to WalkForward/SideStepRight/TurnRight with negated speed at 10123-10150, and SIGNED_MOTION_SPEED is default-on (1360-1367). `_fireHook` hard-drops `(hook.direction | 0) === -1` (15767).
- Retail: execute_hooks (acclient.c:339683-339698) fires `if (!v5 || dir == v5)`. The reverse branch of update_internal (340730-340759) calls `execute_hooks(get_part_frame(v6), -1)` for each frame left going down, so Both and Backward hooks fire and low_frame never fires. advance_to_next_animation with quantum >= 0 takes the forward-list branch: GetNext or first_cyclic, then get_starting_frame (high+1-0.0002 for negative framerate, 341016-341025).
- OpenAC Reverse_DescendingHooks_BackwardDirection (CSequenceUpdateTests.cs:147-157) matches. OpenAC's GetStartingFrame lacks the -eps (AnimSequenceNode.cs:51), as the finding notes.

The cited mechanism is wrong. Retail does not reverse a running cycle with multiply_cyclic_animation_fr(-1):
- GetObjectSequence takes the in-place change_cycle_speed path only `if (motion == mtype2 && same_sign(speed_mod, v7->substate_mod) && has_anims)` (acclient.c:337773).
- A sign flip falls into the else branch (337784-337834): remove_cyclic_anims, relay links (re-picked when `!same_sign`, 337786), then `add_motion(cycle, speed_mod)`.
- add_motion (337431) builds each node with `operator*(AnimData, speed)` (341051), which only scales framerate and does NOT swap low/high. The node then starts at get_starting_frame = high+1-eps.
- multiply_framerate's low/high swap (340968-340979) is unreachable for a sign flip, because change_cycle_speed only sees same-sign ratios or 0. If it ever ran, swapping low/high together with a negative-rate get_starting_frame would play nothing sensible.
verify.corrections:
1. Retail re-sequences on a sign flip: relay links, then the cycle restarted from its last frame and playing backward. Holtburger's in-place phase continuation is a deliberate approximation; the PARITY lead says 'Owner 2026-10-05: backwards walk, strafe = perfect'. Keep it, and fix only the missing hooks.
2. A Rust signed `rate` plus multiplyCyclicFramerate is not needed for hooks. A JS-only frame-index walk in the reverse branch is enough for the (single-node) locomotion cycles.
3. The finding's claim about bake-negated segments is correct. A runtime-reverse gate of {0, -1} on a negated hook equals the original {0, +1}, which is right because double reversal is forward playback.
verify.implementation_notes:
Do this after csequence-1 and csequence-2, which define the cursor and frame-exit semantics.

1. In the reverse branch, read `oldGf = lo.seq.globalFrameIndex` before seekPhase and `newGf` after it.
2. Compute the frames LEFT in descending order, using a pure helper in hook_windows.js: `framesLeftReverse(oldGf, newGf, segStarts, segCounts, numFrames)`.
   - No wrap (newGf <= oldGf): oldGf down to newGf+1.
   - Wrap (single node): oldGf down to 1, then numFrames-1 down to newGf+1.
   - Exclude every segment START frame. In runtime reverse that frame is the node's last frame (retail low_frame never fires).
3. Fire those frames' hooks in that order with dir = -1. Change `_fireHook(inst, hook, audioMgr, cache, dir = 1)` to gate `const d = hook.direction | 0; if ((d === 1 || d === -1) && d !== dir) return;`. This keeps the fail-soft behaviour for undefined and -2.
4. Carry dir through the HOOK_DRAIN_ON queue records (`{kind: "hook", hook, dir}`) and through the drain at 15304-15312.
5. After firing, set `lo.lastHookTime` to the current frame time.
6. Escape flag `?reverseCycleHooks` (default-ON, `!== "off"`).

Tests: `node test_hook_windows.mjs` cases for framesLeftReverse:
- 4-frame node from 3 to 2 leaves [3].

title: A cycle swap that carries phase, or a resume after backing up, fires a burst of hooks; reverse cycle playback fires none
decomp_evidence: In retail, hooks fire only from frames crossed inside CSequence::update_internal; changing the playhead position never fires hooks. The backward branch (acclient.c:340746 `for (...; _floor(*_frame_number) < (double)v6; --v6)` → :340759 `execute_hooks(..., -1)`) fires Both (0) and Backward (-1) hooks for every frame left while moving down. execute_hooks gate is at :339694-339696. WalkBackward, SideStepLeft and TurnLeft are the forward cycles played at negative speed, so they take this branch.

holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js:9239 `try { seq.seekPhase(prev.seq.phase); } catch (_) {}`, then :9249 `hooks: ..., lastHookTime: -1`. The next `_drainUnifiedHooks` fires (-1, ft[gf]], i.e. every hook from frame 0 to the carried phase in one tick. The negative-step branch (:15141-15152) seeks the phase backward, then sets `lo.lastHookTime = -1; // no reverse footfall spam`: nothing fires while backing up, and the first non-negative step on the same installed cycle bursts (-1, curT]. `_fireHook` (:15767, `if ((hook.direction | 0) === -1) return;`) also cannot fire a Backward hook in any case.
discrepancy: A walk→run/idle swap without a link (carryPhase) and a backstep→forward resume both replay, in one frame, every hook between frame 0 and the current phase. Retail fires none of these. Cycles played backward (backstep, left strafe, left turn) are silent, while retail fires their Both and Backward hooks per crossed frame.
proposed_change: (1) In `_installUnifiedLoco` (entities.js ~9238-9250), when a phase was carried, set `lastHookTime = (d.frameTimes?.[seq.globalFrameIndex] ?? 0)` instead of -1. With anim-hooks-1's retiming, the current frame's own hooks then fire when it is left. In the negative-step branch, replace `lo.lastHookTime = -1` with `lo.lastHookTime = ft[lo.seq.globalFrameIndex]`. (2) Reverse firing: read `prevGf = lo.seq.globalFrameIndex` before `seekPhase`. After the seek, walk the frames crossed downward (prevGf down to gf+1, wrapping over the cycle's frame count). Fire hooks from the `hooksByFrame` index built in anim-hooks-1, using retail's backward rule: include each segment's last frame and skip its first frame. Add a `dir` argument to `_fireHooksInRange` and `_fireHook` (default +1) so the gate becomes `direction === 0 || direction === dir`. Reverse-baked segments already negate their directions (lib.rs ~8745), so the same rule holds for them.

(a) Install WALK with Both hooks on frames 0-3, advance to phase 0.5, then setMotion RUN (carryPhase): `_fireHook` is not called on the swap tick. (b) Negative gait step over a cycle with a Both hook on frame 3 and a Forward-only hook on frame 2: crossing 3→2 fires the Both hook once and never the Forward one; turning the step positive again fires nothing until a frame is crossed.

The negative-step branch (:15141-15153) seekPhases backward and sets `lo.lastHookTime = -1` without draining. A later positive step on the same installed cycle bursts (-1, curT]. title: CallPES animation hook uses a wall-clock setTimeout that can attach to a respawned object with the same guid

With delta >= 0.0002 it queues an FPHook delayed by RollDice(0, delta) on the OBJECT's own `hooks` list. process_hooks (:318641) runs that list during the object's update on PhysicsTimer, so it dies with the object. Otherwise it calls `if (this->cell) play_script_internal(pes)`. CallPESHook::Execute is at :342468.

A simpler option is to call `this._executeScriptHook(inst.guid >>> 0, inst.root, 0, hook, 0, -1)` after adding the identity check there too. title: Jump launch planar velocity is the uncapped ground vector, not retail get_leave_ground_velocity (capped at 4 x run_rate), on BOTH jump arms
decomp_evidence: CMotionInterp::jump (acclient.c:344224-344256) -> CPhysicsObj::set_on_walkable(0) -> MovementManager::LeaveGround -> CMotionInterp::LeaveGround (:344457-344489): `CMotionInterp::get_leave_ground_velocity(v1, &local_velocity); CPhysicsObj::set_local_velocity(v1->physics_obj, &local_velocity, 1);` runs for EVERY jump. get_leave_ground_velocity (:343806-343842) = get_state_velocity + vz, falling back to the physics velocity only when |x|,|y| AND |vz| are all under 0.0002. With vz >= 2.62 a jump never falls back. get_state_velocity (:343539-343594) renormalizes the magnitude to run_rate*4.0. ClientCombatSystem::DoJump (:408178-408191) then packs `CPhysicsObj::get_local_physics_velocity` into the JumpPack, so the wire carries the capped vector too.
openac_evidence: MotionInterpreter.cs:929-949 LeaveGround: `var velocity = GetLeaveGroundVelocity(); PhysicsObj.set_local_velocity(velocity, autonomous: true);`. GetLeaveGroundVelocity is at :745-760 and the get_state_velocity cap at :465-469 (`if (len > maxSpeed ...) velocity = Normalize(velocity) * maxSpeed`). PlayerMovementController.cs:2012-2013 calls `_motion.LeaveGround()` on every ground-to-air edge, jump or walk-off. Pinned by tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Physics/MotionInterpreterGroundLifecycleTests.cs:205 LeaveGround_VelocityCarriesGetLeaveGroundVelocity_WithNonzeroJumpExtent.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/system.rs:3642-3651. The charged arm uses `self.manual_intent_velocity(world)`, which at :8341-8353 returns `interpreted_velocity_for_state(...)`, the uncapped ground form. The non-charged arm uses `world.local_player_runtime_kinematics().map(|(_, v, _)| Vector3::new(v.x, v.y, vz))`, the realized velocity. The local arc uses `current_planar_velocity`, which begin_jump leaves untouched (holtburger-world player/types.rs:2020-2025), so it is the last uncapped grounded store. By contrast the walk-off path already uses the retail form: stamp_leave_ground_velocity (system.rs:1735-1753) -> motion_interp.rs:1849-1866 leave_ground_velocity_for_state.
discrepancy: Retail caps the launch at |v| = 4*run_rate. Holtburger launches with the ground diagonal sum. Below the strafe clamp knee (run_rate < 2.40) the ratio is sqrt(16 + 1.56^2)/4 = 1.073, so running-diagonal jumps launch 7.3% hot: 8.48 vs 7.90 m/s at the rig rate of 1.9758. At rate 4.5 the excess is 2.2% (18.39 vs 18.0). Both the local trajectory lock and the JumpPack velocity that ACE applies via set_local_velocity (and therefore what observers see) carry the error. The non-charged arm also departs from retail on slopes and against walls, because it uses the collision-reduced realized velocity where retail uses the intended state velocity. A no-key jump while residual-sliding launches with the residual, where retail launches with (0,0,vz).
proposed_change: In MovementSystem::execute_jump_release, replace the whole lateral_velocity branch (system.rs:3642-3651) with this: when the active drive is Manual(state), compute `let v = leave_ground_velocity_for_state(heading, state, &caps, Vector3::zero())`. Pass zero as the integrator fallback because vz > eps disables retail's fallback (:343826), which resolves the caveat left open in Handoff 1. Then set `world.player.current_planar_velocity = (v.x, v.y, 0)` and use `(v.x, v.y, vz)` for the pack, for charged AND non-charged releases. Keep the runtime-kinematics fallback only when there is no manual drive or no capabilities (autonomous MoveTo). Optionally switch manual_intent_velocity to the capped form as well, or delete it once this is its only caller. Gate it behind a const, as was done for USE_LEAVE_GROUND_VELOCITY.
test_plan: New async #[test] in crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/system/tests.rs, next to execute_jump_release_without_charge_is_not_charging (:6118): `execute_jump_release_launch_is_capped_state_velocity`. Assert |current_planar_velocity| == 4.0 (±1e-4), not 4.293, and that the sent JumpPack local (x,y) equals the capped body vector. Add a second case with no keys held: planar launch == 0. Run with `cargo test -p holtburger-core execute_jump_release_launch` (orchestrator only, inside capped-build).

title: Remote TurnToHeading node can stall forever: the scene clamps the turn exactly onto the node heading, but retail completion needs heading_greater (strict overshoot)
decomp_evidence: MoveToManager::BeginTurnToHeading acclient.c:345456 issues TurnRight (0x6500000D) when heading_diff(node, curr) ∈ (eps, 180]. The body then rotates by motion omega every frame (CSequence::apply_physics), with no stop at the target. MoveToManager::HandleTurnToHeading :345712: `if ( heading_greater(curr_heading, node_heading, current_command) ) { set_heading(node, 1); pop; _StopMotion; BeginNextNode }` — completion is detected by OVERSHOOT and then snapped. heading_greater :344715 is strict: for TurnRight, `result = (x < y || x == y) == 0`, i.e. x > y.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Physics/Motion/MoveToManager.cs:704-718 `if (MoveToMath.HeadingGreater(heading, head.Heading, cmd)) { ... _setHeading(head.Heading, true); RemovePendingActionsHead(); ... BeginNextNode(); }`. The turn itself is an interp motion (`_DoMotion` :869-877 → `_interp.DoInterpretedMotion`) that the sequencer integrates past the target. tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Physics/Motion/MoveToManagerTurnToHeadingTests.cs:124-142 HandleTurnToHeading_Arrival_SnapsHeadingAndSendsTrue sets heading 91 for a 90 node ("just past the target") before arrival fires.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/scene.rs:5869-5903 (D5 turn block): `let mut diff = (drive.heading_rad - current) % TAU; ... let max = rate * quantum; let turn = diff.clamp(-max, max); if turn.abs() > 1e-5 { body.pose.rotation = Quaternion::from_heading(current + turn); ...}` — the last step lands exactly on the target, and later steps under 1e-5 rad do nothing. crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/move_to.rs:1026-1028 `if heading_greater(curr_heading, node_heading, self.current_command) { ... out.set_heading = Some(node_heading.to_radians()); ...}` and params.rs:49-56 `heading_greater` (strict `!le` for TurnRight). system.rs:9820-9823 maps MoveToSteer::Turn to `RemoteMoveToDrive { heading_rad: normalize_heading(heading_deg.to_radians()), forward: None }`, dropping the TurnRight/TurnLeft command.
discrepancy: The node heading goes degrees → radians → quaternion → atan2 → degrees, so the clamped final heading lands within about 1e-5° of the node with either sign. For TurnRight nodes it is often not strictly greater, so heading_greater stays false, the node never pops and the scene never turns further. This affects the leading TurnToHeading node of every remote MoveToObject/MoveToPosition, plus TurnToObject/TurnToHeading. While stalled, drive stays Some(Turn), so there is no client walk (scene.rs:5680 `Some(_) => Vector3::zero()`), the NETSYNC-3 interpreted turn is suppressed (5840 `body.remote_moveto.is_none()`), and keep_heading=true ignores wire headings. The mob slides on interp facing a frozen direction until the next UpdateMotion, which is the D5 symptom the drive was meant to fix. TurnLeft arrivals complete because their test is non-strict.
proposed_change: Make the remote turn a motion, not a clamped turn-to. (a) Add the command to the steer, e.g. `MoveToSteer::Turn { heading_deg, hold_key, command }` (current_command, TurnRight or TurnLeft). Add `turn: Option<f32>` (signed: +1 TurnRight / −1 TurnLeft) to RemoteMoveToDrive in types.rs, filled in drive_remote_movetos. (b) In the scene turn block, rotate by `sign × rate × quantum` WITHOUT clamping to drive.heading_rad, so the body overshoots like retail. The next drive_remote_movetos tick sees heading_greater and applies the existing set_heading snap (set_remote_moveto snap_heading). Keep the shortest-arc clamp only as a fallback when `turn` is None, for compatibility.
test_plan: Rust #[test] in crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/tests.rs, `remote_moveto_turn_right_overshoots_node_heading`: body heading 0, drive turn=+1 with a node 2° away, step 1/30 s. Assert the heading passed the node, which fails deterministically on the current clamp. Rust #[test] in crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/movement_manager.rs tests, `remote_turn_node_completes_then_walks`: TurnRight MoveToPosition 0°→90° 20 m away. Loop drive_remote_movetos + step_remote_position_managers(1/30) for 3 s and assert the steer reaches Walk and the heading equals the node (snap). Both are run by the orchestrator (cargo); no node test applies.
already_tracked: no (D5 landed in 7972f3e8/e6b1e7c9; PARITY-STATUS still lists 'HIGH D5 ... face stale heading' as open — stale; this stall is a new defect inside the landed D5)

verify.reasons: Decomp: heading_greater (:344715) gives `result = (v3||v4)==0` for TurnRight (strict x>y within 180°) and `(v3||v4)!=0` for any other motion (x<=y). HandleTurnToHeading (:345712) pops the node and snaps only when heading_greater holds. The else branch only increments fail_progress_count, and nothing in the decomp reads fail_progress_count to cancel, so a miss is not recovered. holtburger handle_turn_to_heading (move_to.rs ~1016-1047) mirrors this exactly. drive_remote_movetos maps `MoveToSteer::Turn { heading_deg, .. }` to `RemoteMoveToDrive { heading_rad: normalize_heading(heading_deg.to_radians()), forward: None }` and drops the command. The scene D5 turn block (scene.rs:5869-5903) clamps `turn = diff.clamp(-max, max)` and skips anything under 1e-5 rad, so the last slice lands on the node heading. Quaternion::from_heading/to_heading (holtburger-common math.rs:156-200) go through `450 - deg` in f32, so the round-trip error is about 1e-5° with either sign. If the result is not strictly past the node, the node never pops and the scene never turns again. Nothing else rotates the body. NETSYNC-3 is skipped while remote_moveto is Some (:5840). The near-contact reconcile interpolates with keep_heading = remote_moving_to (:5481). Every MoveToObject/MoveToPosition starts with a TurnToHeading(heading_to_target) node (move_to.rs build_move_nodes ~794). Not tracked anywhere; PARITY 'HIGH D5' is stale since 7972f3e8/e6b1e7c9.
verify.corrections: TurnLeft stalls too. Its test is `x <= y`. Approaching from above, a clamped landing that rounds to node + ε fails just as TurnRight fails at node − ε. The non-strict compare only rescues exact equality. A completely unclamped turn also has a hazard. The pump's on_contact is `remote_arc.is_none() && last_wire_contact != Some(false)` (remote_moveto_view), but the scene turn gate is only `remote_arc.is_none()`. A body whose wire says no contact would then spin forever, because UseTime never observes the overshoot. Use an overshoot-then-hold step rather than unbounded rotation.
verify.implementation_notes: (1) move_to.rs: give MoveToSteer::Turn the active command, e.g. `Turn { heading_deg, hold_key, command: u32 }` filled from self.current_command in current_steer. (2) holtburger-world spatial/types.rs: add `turn: Option<f32>` to RemoteMoveToDrive, signed +1.0 TurnRight / -1.0 TurnLeft (shared with moveto-3). Update every constructor (system.rs drive_remote_movetos; tests.rs ~4192, ~4405, ~4456). (3) system.rs drive_remote_movetos: for Turn, set `turn: Some(if command == MOTION_TURN_LEFT { -1.0 } else { 1.0 })`. (4) scene.rs D5 turn block, when `drive.turn = Some(s)` and forward is None: `d = wrap_pi(drive.heading_rad - current) * s` is the signed remaining angle in the command direction. Const OVERSHOOT = 1e-3 rad (about 0.057°, well above the ~1e-5° round-trip noise). If d <= -OVERSHOOT, do nothing (already past; hold until the pump snaps). Otherwise `step = (d + OVERSHOOT).min(rate * quantum)` and rotate by `s * step`. Keep the existing shortest-arc clamp when `turn` is None. The pump's next tick then sees heading_greater and applies the existing set_heading snap (set_remote_moveto snap_heading). Gate the turn on the same contact view the pump uses (`body.last_wire_contact != Some(false)`) so a body the pump cannot step never rotates. (5) Fix the stale `keep_heading = false this stage` comment near scene.rs:5469. Escape: ?remoteMoveTo=off. This is a defect inside landed D5, so a separate flag is optional; if wanted, `?remoteTurnOvershoot=off` keeps the old clamp. Tests (orchestrator cargo, no node test applies). In crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/tests.rs add `remote_moveto_turn_overshoots_then_holds`. For each sign: heading 0, node 2° away in the command direction. Step 1/30 s and assert the heading is strictly past the node by ≤ OVERSHOOT + 1e-6. Step 10 more slices and assert no further rotation. In crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/movement_manager.rs tests add `remote_turn_node_completes_then_walks`, using the existing remote_moveto_pump_steers_the_remote_body scaffolding. Use a TurnRight case (target bearing +90°) and a TurnLeft case. Loop drive_remote_movetos + step_remote_position_managers(1/30) for 3 s and assert the steer reaches Walk (drive.forward.is_some()) with heading == node after the snap. Needs a wasm rebuild.

title: Remote MoveTo moves the body along the bearing to its target instead of along its facing; it turns continuously instead of using the 20° aux-turn deadband, and it still turns while an interp node owns the offset
decomp_evidence: MoveToManager::HandleMoveToPosition acclient.c:345577: `if ( v7 <= 20.0 || v7 >= 360.0 - 20.0 ) { _StopMotion(aux_command) } else { v8 = TurnRight; if (v7 >= 180.0) v8 = TurnLeft; if (v8 != aux_command) _DoMotion(v8) }`. While aligned within 20° there is NO rotation, and the body advances by its RunForward/WalkForward cycle in its own local frame (CSequence::apply_physics, composed in UpdatePositionInternal). InterpolationManager::adjust_offset :389178: while a node is active on contact, `if ( v3->keep_heading ) Frame::set_heading(&adjustment, 0.0); Frame::operator=(offset, &adjustment);` REPLACES the whole offset, so the animation's aux turn is discarded too.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Runtime/Physics/RuntimeRemotePhysicsUpdater.cs:176-179 (root-motion origin when on walkable) and :221-222 (`pmDelta.Origin = scaledRootMotionLocalOrigin; pmDelta.Orientation = rootMotionLocalFrame.Orientation;`). Then :723-733 ApplyPositionManagerDelta: `body.Position += Vector3.Transform(delta.Origin, body.Orientation)` — movement along the body's own facing. MoveToManager.cs:614-628 is the 20°/340° aux deadband. ACE server mirrors it (ACE.Server/Physics/Managers/MoveToManager.cs:433 `if (diff > 20.0f && diff < 340.0f)`), so the server's monster path follows retail's.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/scene.rs:5676-5680: `Some(RemoteMoveToDrive { heading_rad, forward: Some(run) }) if walk => { let speed = ...; Quaternion::from_heading(heading_rad).rotate_vector(Vector3::new(0.0, speed, 0.0)) }` — the translation uses the steer heading, not body.pose.rotation. system.rs:9800-9817 sets heading_rad to the direct bearing to the target every tick. scene.rs:5869-5903 turns toward that exact bearing every slice, and unlike the NETSYNC-3 block (5841-5848 `let interp_owns = body.position_manager.queue_active() && ...`) has no interp gate. The state machine does compute aux_command (move_to.rs:960-975), but MoveToSteer::Walk (move_to.rs:217-221) drops it.
discrepancy: Holtburger mobs pursue perfectly and slide sideways toward the target while their facing lags. Retail and the ACE server run along their facing, tolerate up to 20° of error, and arc through aux turns. The client path therefore differs systematically from the server path, which means larger corrections at each 5 Hz UpdatePosition. The body also rotates during interp nodes, where retail's keep_heading replace freezes it.
proposed_change: Carry aux_command in `MoveToSteer::Walk { ..., aux: u32 }` and add a signed `turn` to RemoteMoveToDrive (shared with moveto-2). In ground_moves, compute walk_v from `body.pose.rotation.rotate_vector(Vector3::new(0.0, ±speed, 0.0))`, using the body's facing (negative for WalkBackwards). In the D5 turn block, rotate only when `drive.turn` is Some (aux active for Walk, the node command for Turn), and skip it while `queue_active() && remote_arc.is_none() && last_wire_contact.unwrap_or(true)` (the interp-owns gate NETSYNC-3 already uses).
test_plan: Rust #[test]s in crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/tests.rs (orchestrator cargo): `remote_moveto_walk_advances_along_facing` (heading 0, bearing 15°, run, turn None → displacement direction == facing, heading unchanged); `remote_moveto_aux_turn_only_outside_deadband` (bearing 30° → turn applied; 15° → none); `remote_moveto_turn_idles_while_interp_owns` (queue active + contact → heading unchanged). Extend the existing `remote_moveto_drive_runs_toward_its_heading` (tests.rs:4188) accordingly.
already_tracked: partially: PARITY remote_motion open 'HIGH D5 ... chasing mobs face stale heading, overshoot' (D5 itself landed; this is its realization)

verify.reasons: Decomp HandleMoveToPosition (:345577) computes the desired heading delta. It stops aux when `v7 <= 20.0 || v7 >= 360.0 - 20.0` and otherwise _DoMotion(TurnRight/TurnLeft). Translation comes from the RunForward/WalkForward motion in the object's own frame. InterpolationManager::adjust_offset (:389178) on contact with an active position node does `if ( v3->keep_heading ) Frame::set_heading(&adjustment, 0.0); Frame::operator=(offset, &adjustment)`. That replaces the whole offset with zero rotation (Frame::set_heading(0) gives direction (0,1) = identity yaw), discarding motion turns. ACE server MoveToManager.cs:433 `if (diff > 20.0f && diff < 340.0f)` matches. OpenAC MoveToManager.cs ~604-628 has the same deadband, and RuntimeRemotePhysicsUpdater.ApplyPositionManagerDelta (~723-733) moves along body.Orientation. In holtburger, scene.rs:5676-5679 builds walk_v from `Quaternion::from_heading(heading_rad)` (the steer heading). drive_remote_movetos sets heading_rad to the direct planar bearing to the target every tick. The D5 turn block (:5869-5903) turns toward that bearing every slice and has no interp-owns gate, unlike NETSYNC-3 at :5841-5843. MoveToSteer::Walk is `{ target, away, run }` (move_to.rs:217-221), so the aux_command computed in handle_move_to_position is dropped.
verify.corrections: The citations hold. Two consequences to add: the existing test remote_moveto_drive_runs_toward_its_heading (spatial/tests.rs:4188) asserts the body runs 0.4 m east while starting at heading 0, which fails by design under a facing-based walk and must be rewritten. And moveto-2, moveto-3 and moveto-5 all change RemoteMoveToDrive, so they should land as one change.
verify.implementation_notes: Land together with moveto-2 (shared `turn: Option<f32>` on RemoteMoveToDrive). (1) move_to.rs: `MoveToSteer::Walk { target, away, run, aux: u32 }` with aux = self.aux_command (0, TurnRight or TurnLeft). (2) system.rs drive_remote_movetos: keep heading_rad for diagnostics. Set `turn = match aux { MOTION_TURN_RIGHT => Some(1.0), MOTION_TURN_LEFT => Some(-1.0), _ => None }`. (3) scene.rs ground_moves (~5674-5680): for `forward: Some(run)` use `body.pose.rotation.rotate_vector(Vector3::new(0.0, speed, 0.0))`, the body's own facing, instead of from_heading(heading_rad). An away walk already has its facing reversed by the turn node and aux heading (get_desired_heading 0/180), so no negation is needed for WalkForward. (4) D5 turn block: for Walk drives, rotate by `s * rate * quantum` only when `drive.turn = Some(s)`; the deadband lives in the state machine, which re-evaluates every tick. Skip the whole D5 turn (Walk and Turn) while `body.position_manager.queue_active() && body.remote_arc.is_none() && body.last_wire_contact.unwrap_or(true)`, the same interp_owns predicate NETSYNC-3 uses. Also skip it when `last_wire_contact == Some(false)`, matching the pump's contact view, so aux cannot spin a body the pump is not stepping. Flag: `?remoteMoveToFacing=off` (Rust parse fn `!= "remoteMoveToFacing=off"`, scene setter, url-flags.md row next to remoteMoveTo) restores bearing-walk with continuous turn. Tests (orchestrator cargo, crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/tests.rs): `remote_moveto_walk_advances_along_facing` (heading h0, bearing h0+15°, run, turn None: displacement parallel to the facing, heading unchanged); `remote_moveto_aux_turn_only_when_commanded` (turn Some(+1): heading increases by rate*1.5*q; None: unchanged); `remote_moveto_turn_idles_while_interp_owns` (queue active + contact: heading unchanged). Rewrite remote_moveto_drive_runs_toward_its_heading to start facing east. In movement_manager.rs tests, add an assertion that the aux command appears in the steer when the bearing is 30° off and is absent at 15°. Needs a wasm rebuild.

title: Remote MoveTo animation phase (turn-in-place / run / walk / stop) still comes from the JS COL-20 heading-error heuristic, which D5's heading rows now neutralize
decomp_evidence: Each MoveTo phase is a motion on the mover's CMotionInterp, and through it the motion table and animation. BeginTurnToHeading :345489-345510 `_DoMotion(TurnRight/TurnLeft)`. BeginMoveForward :345371-345425 `_DoMotion(get_command(...))` → Walk/Run. HandleMoveToPosition aux `_DoMotion(TurnRight/Left)` (turn modifier while running). Arrival in BeginNextNode :345521-345545: `CleanUp; CPhysicsObj::StopCompletely` → Ready. MoveToManager::_DoMotion :344753 = `adjust_motion` + `CMotionInterp::DoInterpretedMotion`.
openac_evidence: RuntimeRemoteArming.cs:404-447 RouteServerMoveTo → `movement.PerformMovement(walk)`. The MoveToManager's `_DoMotion` (MoveToManager.cs:869-877) drives `_interp.DoInterpretedMotion`, whose sink is the remote's animation sequencer (RemoteInboundMotionDispatcher.Apply takes `IInterpretedMotionSink? animationSink`), so the clip always matches the node.

title: Ballistic projectiles have no environment collision (only an outdoor terrain stop); retail sweeps every missile through a CTransition each step
decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::UpdateObjectInternal (acclient.c:322719): for every ACTIVE object with collision spheres, after UpdatePositionInternal it applies ALIGN_PATH (:322800-322804), then `v15 = CPhysicsObj::transition(v2, &v2->m_position, &new_pos, 0)` (:322812) and `SetPositionInternal(v2, v16)` (:322829). If the transition fails, the old origin is kept and cached_velocity is zeroed (:322832-322846). On contact, CPhysicsObj::report_environment_collision (:320194) and report_object_collision (:320228) both clear MISSILE|ALIGN_PATH|PATH_CLIPPED (`state & 0xFFFFFCBF`, :320222 / :320290). handle_all_collisions (:321808) then reflects the velocity by elasticity (default 0.05) or zeroes it for INELASTIC. So the retail client stops a missile at walls, objects and creatures by itself. ACE confirms this in SpellProjectile.cs:232-235: it sends an extra VectorUpdate because a SetState that arrives early would otherwise leave a 'ghost' projectile on the client that 'continue[s] to sail through the target'.

The only collision is `if (PROJECTILE_TERRAIN_STOP_ON && inst._ballisticTerrainOk) { const gz = _terrainZAt(pos.x, pos.y); ... }` (:14538-14544). `_ballisticTerrainOk` can only become true outdoors: `if (PROJECTILE_TERRAIN_STOP_ON && (inst._outdoorCellIdx & 0xffff) < 0x0100)` (:5067). Indoors and against buildings, statics and doors nothing stops the bolt before the ACE impact VectorUpdate in setVelocity (:10989-11050). The sphere sweeps already exist in wasm and the camera uses them: src/lib.rs:37884 sweepSphereAgainstBuildingMesh, :37919 sweepSphereAgainstStatics, :37967 sweepSphereAgainstCellMesh, :38004 sweepSphereAgainstCellStatics, :38048 sweepSphereAgainstEntities. CollisionHit carries t, x/y/z and normalX/Y/Z (:34443-34490). The chained call pattern is scene3d/camera.js:1475 `_clipCameraAgainstWorld`.
discrepancy: Retail collides a missile with the environment, statics and objects locally on every step, so it stops at the wall or target. Holtburger keeps integrating through building walls, dungeon walls, furniture and closed doors until the server's zero-velocity VectorUpdate and NoDraw arrive. The overshoot is speed times latency: a 20 m/s bolt at 100 ms RTT ends up about 1-2 m past the wall, and the Explode PlayScript then plays on the far side. Indoors there is no stop at all.
proposed_change: In `_tickBallisticProjectiles`, record p0 before each substep and, after integrating to p1, call a new helper `_sweepProjectileStep(inst, p0, p1)` that does the following. (a) Outdoors (cell low 16 bits < 0x100): call `sh.sweepSphereAgainstBuildingMesh` and `sh.sweepSphereAgainstStatics` with the projectile's own landblock/cell id (from inst._outdoorCellIdx, or derived from pos/192). (b) Indoors: call `sh.sweepSphereAgainstCellMesh` and `sh.sweepSphereAgainstCellStatics` with `getRenderSet(1)` (the same cell list the camera uses). (c) Always: call `sh.sweepSphereAgainstEntities(..., range = |p1-p0| + 5)` for closed doors. These are BSP-only, so the caster and creatures are excluded automatically, as in OpenAC's self-shadow rule. Keep the hit with the smallest t, accepting only hits with t > 0 and normal·(p1−p0) < 0, so a launch point embedded in a doorway does not kill the bolt. Free every hit box, as freeHit does in camera.js. On a hit, set pos = p0 + (p1−p0)·t − a 0.05 m backoff along the direction, then call `_stopBallisticProjectile(inst)` and continue. Retail's 5% elastic rebound after MISSILE is cleared is not visible before NoDraw, so a plain stop is enough. Use a fixed radius PROJECTILE_SWEEP_RADIUS = 0.1 m as a documented stand-in for the Setup sphere (OpenAC's arrow sphere is 0.102 times scale). verify.corrections:
1. The proposed outdoor arm `sweepSphereAgainstStatics` must NOT be used. It is a coarse AABB test: SpatialScene::sweep_sphere_against_statics (scene.rs:4024) calls physics.rs:1541-1563 `sweep_sphere_against_static_aabbs`, which runs `entry.aabb.inflate(radius)` and then a ray-vs-AABB slab test against each static's whole AABB. A bolt would stop on a tree canopy, sign or prop bounding box that retail and ACE fly past, freezing the bolt and playing the explosion short of a target the server says was hit. That is a false positive, which is worse than today's false negative, since ACE's impact still arrives. The JS-only fix is limited to the building mesh (per-triangle physics_polygons), EnvCell mesh, EnvCell stab BSPs and BSP entities (doors). Precise outdoor statics need a new BSP export (wasm), as a follow-up.
2. The blanket `accept t > 0` rule is wrong. sweep_sphere_against_triangles (physics.rs:1680-1684) returns target t=0 whenever the start lies within radius of a triangle's plane. It also orients the normal toward the start side (physics.rs:1707-1713), so `normal·dir < 0` is always true for triangle hits and adds nothing. Ignoring every t≈0 hit lets a bolt whose step ended touching a wall tunnel through on the next step. Ignore t≈0 hits only during the launch window: the first substep, or until the bolt has travelled more than 2·radius from its spawn point.
3. sweepSphereAgainstBuildingMesh indexes a single landblock (`building_triangles_for_landblock(lb & 0xFFFF0000)`, scene.rs:5091). Derive the landblock from the segment, `((floor(x/192)&0xff)<<24 | (floor(y/192)&0xff)<<16)>>>0`, and sweep both p0's and p1's landblocks when they differ.

title: Projectile gravity arc uses semi-implicit Euler instead of retail's exact v*q + 1/2*a*q^2, so the arc depends on frame rate and sags below ACE's path
decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::UpdatePhysicsInternal (acclient.c:317701): the position offset is taken from the OLD (clamped) velocity plus a half step, `v8 = v6 * quantum; v9 = v8 * quantum; ... w.z = result.z + w.z * quantum * quantum` with v6/w.z = 0.5·accel (:317757-317769). Only after that does it apply `v += a·q` (:317771-317776). For constant gravity this is exact for any step size. ALIGN_PATH heads along the step's chord: `diff = new_origin - old_origin; Normalize; Frame::set_vector_heading` (:322800-322804).
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Physics/PhysicsBody.cs:339 `Position += Velocity * dt + Acceleration * (0.5f * dt * dt);` then :342 `Velocity += Acceleration * dt;`. ProjectilePhysicsStepper.cs:213-222 takes AlignPath from the displacement. The test tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Physics/ProjectilePhysicsStepperTests.cs:137 Advance_GravityUsesFinalPhysicsState_NotParsedAcceleration pins z = z0 + 0.5·g·q^2 and vz = g·q. :175 Advance_AlignPathUsesActualThreeDimensionalDisplacement pins the chord heading.
holt_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/scene3d/entities.js:14521-14530: `const step = remaining > 0.1 ? 0.1 : remaining; ... if (inst._ballisticGravity) lv.vz += PROJECTILE_GRAVITY_Z * step; pos.x += lv.vx * step; pos.y += lv.vy * step; pos.z += lv.vz * step;`. The comment at :14522-14524 claims this matches 'the retail arc'. At :14534 `_alignToVelocity(inst, lv)` uses the end-of-frame velocity, not the chord.
discrepancy: Each substep drops an extra 0.5·g·q^2, so the total error is 0.5·g·q·T, and it depends on frame rate. That is 8 cm low after a 1 s flight at 60 fps, about 0.4 m for a 2.5 s arrow at 30 fps, and 0.49 m per second at the 0.1 s substep cap (≤10 fps). ACE solves the arrow's launch velocity for an exact parabola and integrates it retail-style on the server. The client arrow therefore runs below the server's path. With the client terrain stop, a long or downhill shot can hit the ground short of a target that the server says it reached.
proposed_change: In the substep loop at entities.js:14520-14531, replace the vertical update with the retail order: `const az = inst._ballisticGravity ? PROJECTILE_GRAVITY_Z : 0; pos.x += lv.vx*step; pos.y += lv.vy*step; pos.z += lv.vz*step + 0.5*az*step*step; lv.vz += az*step;`. Fix the :14522-14524 comment. Optionally keep the last substep's chord (pos minus its pre-step value) and pass it to `_alignToVelocity` in place of `lv`, to match retail's chord heading; the difference is under 0.5° at bolt speeds. No flag is needed: this is a pure accuracy fix to an exact closed form, and it composes with physupd-1.
test_plan: New test tests/projectile_ballistic_arc.test.mjs. Reuse the brace-matching harness from tests/projectile_spin.test.mjs, which lifts `_tickBallisticProjectiles`, `_stopBallisticProjectile`, `_setProjectileLightsOn`, `_spinProjectile` and `_alignToVelocity` with PROJECTILE_GRAVITY_Z=-9.8 and terrain stop off. Set up an inst with `_ballistic:true, _ballisticGravity:true, lastVel:{vx:0,vy:20,vz:5}`, `_ballisticLastMs = performance.now()-1000`, run one pass and read T from the consumed time. Assert z ≈ 5T − 4.9T² (1e-3) and vz ≈ 5 − 9.8T. Repeat as ten 0.1 s passes and assert the same z (step-size invariance), which fails today by about 0.5·9.8·0.1·1. title: Incomplete per-object stamp gates: DeleteObject (instance not even parsed, local player not exempt), PickupEvent, ParentEvent, ObjDescEvent ungated; instance leg missing in the movement/vector gates; SetState newer-instance branch never adopts the instance
decomp_evidence:
- SmartBox::HandleDeleteObject (acclient.c:143262-143296): `if ( object_id == this->player_id ) result = 3;` ignores the player. An unknown or newer instance is queued. `else if ( v7 == instance_timestamp )` deletes (143288-143290). An older instance is dropped (result 2).
- HandleObjDescEvent (144356-144392) + UpdateVisualDesc (143302-143330): the instance must be equal and update_times[7] strictly newer.
- HandlePickupEvent (144473-144509) + DoPickupEvent (143483-143500): the instance must be equal and update_times[0] newer.
- HandleParentEvent (144512-144552) + DoParentEvent (143504-143530): the parent's instance must be equal, the child must exist, and the child's update_times[0] must be newer.

discrepancy: Duplicated, reordered or previous-generation lifecycle messages are applied when retail would drop them: a late Delete/Pickup can remove a newer generation, and a stale ObjDesc/Parent can revert appearance or the attachment. title: Same-power duel tiebreak compares raw wire start_time (not rebased to receive time) and lets the incumbent win ties
decomp_evidence: Enchantment::UnPack (acclient.c:502627): `this->_start_time = COERCE_DOUBLE(Timer::cur_time.Cmd) + this->_start_time;` (also applied to _last_time_degraded), so stored times are absolute. Enchantment::Duel (502375): `return v2 > v3 || v2 == v3 && challenger->_start_time < this->_start_time;`, so the incumbent survives only if it has higher power or the challenger is strictly older; an equal start time goes to the challenger. CEnchantmentRegistry::Duel (445675) removes the loser and appends the winner.
openac_evidence: OpenAC is not a retail reference here. src/AcDream.Core/Spells/EnchantmentMath.cs:63-71 dedups by Family and keeps the higher SpellId, with no start-time key. Holtburger's own buffs HUD already stamps receive time (plugins/buffs-hud.js:112-146 receivedAt cache keyed on wire startTime).
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/magic.rs:58 `challenger.start_time > current.start_time` on the raw wire value (strict). player/mutations.rs:599-617 upsert_enchantment and :481 hydrate (`self.enchantments = data.enchantments.clone()`) store the wire start_time unchanged. ACE sends 0 for a fresh cast and negative elapsed seconds for older ones.
discrepancy: Two same-category, same-power layers that arrive in separate MagicUpdateEnchantment events both carry start_time of about 0. Holtburger keeps the one earlier in the Vec (usually the older), while retail keeps the newest. An exact tie goes to the incumbent instead of the challenger. When the two layers' StatModValues differ, the displayed stat can follow the stale layer.
proposed_change: Leave the wire start_time untouched, because the JS buffs HUD keys on it. Add `PlayerState.enchantment_abs_start: HashMap<(u16 spell_id, u16 layer), f64>`, stamped at hydrate/upsert time with a monotonic session clock as `now + wire.start_time` and pruned on remove/purge. verify.reasons:

- Enchantment::Duel (502375): `return inc_power > ch_power || inc_power == ch_power && challenger->_start_time < this->_start_time`, so an exact tie goes to the challenger.

Only the receive-time rebase is correct. A usable clock already exists: WorldState::current_server_time() (state/types.rs:1437). OpenAC is not a reference here (it dedups by higher SpellId).
