title: Dead-session detector keys on game messages, not transport packets, and has no client-stall guard (false disconnects at char select/chargen and after a netWorker main-thread freeze)
decomp_evidence: ClientNet::ProcessConnection (acclient.c:372842) declares the link dead only when `COERCE_DOUBLE(Timer::cur_time.Cmd) - v2->lastDidUseTime_ < 140.0 && Timer::local_time - pReceiver->m_LocalTimeLastGotData > 140.0` (372914-372915), then sets cs_DisconnectReceived. m_LocalTimeLastGotData is stamped for EVERY accepted packet in SharedNet::ProcessPacket (372147-372148), so ack-only and TimeSync packets count. lastDidUseTime_ is the time of the previous net pump (SharedNet::UseTime 369903 `v1->lastDidUseTime_ = now;`; ClientNet::UseTime 370143 runs ProcessConnection before reading the socket). That is the guard: a client that itself stalled for 140 s or more does not blame the server.
openac_evidence: WorldSession.cs:382 `ServerSilenceTimeoutSeconds = 140.0`. IsServerSilent (WorldSession.cs:409-424) returns false when `sincePreviousTurn` is 140 s or more (the client stood still) and otherwise checks `sinceLastInbound > 140`. _lastInboundPacketTicks is written for every admitted datagram (WorldSession.cs:1143), not per game message. Pinned by tests/AcDream.Core.Net.Tests/Transport/ServerSilenceTests.cs `ClientThatStoodStill_ReadsItsSocketBeforeJudgingTheServer` and `SilenceThreshold_IsStrictlyPast140Seconds`.
holt_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:44926-44929 `let inbound_dead = match *last_recv_instant.borrow() { Some(t) => t.elapsed() > Duration::from_secs(90), None => loop_started_at.elapsed() > 60s }`. This runs on every 5 s keepalive tick in all states, and the tokio::select! at 44880 is not biased. The only writer of last_recv_instant is src/session/messages/mod.rs:89, which runs for SessionEvent::Message only: the TimeSync arm (mod.rs:75-83) does `return LoopFlow::Continue` before the stamp. At character select ACE sends no game messages, only TimeSync every 20 s (ace-server NetworkSession.cs:31,203-208) and ack-only packets every 2 s (:32,211-216). holtburger ACKs the TimeSyncs, so ACE keeps the session, but holtburger declares it dead after 90 s. In proxy mode, net_worker.rs:220-225 suppresses only the keepalive send and not this detector, so after a freeze of 90 s or more the keepalive tick can win the select before the worker's queued messages drain. Transport liveness already exists in Session::last_recv_time (crates/holtburger-session/src/session/receive.rs:68) but is unused by the web client. holtburger-core's native loop uses it (runtime.rs:86).
discrepancy: Retail (and OpenAC) judge liveness on any accepted transport packet, over 140 s, and skip the check when the client itself was not pumping. holtburger-web judges on decoded game messages only, over 90 s, with no stall guard. The result is false disconnects: idling at character select or chargen for about 90 s while ACE is healthy, and a ?netWorker (bot/agent) session after a main-thread freeze of 90 s or more, which defeats the point of the worker.
proposed_change: 1) In holtburger-session add `pub const SERVER_SILENCE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(140)` (retail) and `pub fn is_server_silent(&self, previous_check: Instant, now: Instant) -> bool { now.saturating_duration_since(previous_check) < SERVER_SILENCE_TIMEOUT && now.saturating_duration_since(self.last_recv_time) > SERVER_SILENCE_TIMEOUT }`. Optionally move the last_recv_time stamp in receive.rs:68 to after checksum validation, so only accepted packets count, as in retail. 2) In net_worker.rs add `LoopSession::server_silent(&self, prev, now)`: Direct calls s.is_server_silent(prev, now); Proxy returns false, because the worker owns the check. In net_worker_run's keepalive arm, keep a `prev_check` Instant and, when `session.is_server_silent(prev_check, now)`, call worker_post(RX_KIND_DISCONNECT, "server silent 140 s") and return. 3) In lib.rs:44926-44929, replace the last_recv_instant test with `session.server_silent(prev_keepalive_tick, now)`, update prev_keepalive_tick every tick, and keep the 60 s 'never heard anything' handshake branch. last_recv_instant stays as the link-status indicator only. Minimal stopgap if the full change is deferred: move the `*last_recv_instant.borrow_mut() = Some(now)` stamp in session/messages/mod.rs above `match event`, so the 20 s TimeSync keeps char select alive. The bridge's own transport-level 90 s ACE-silence reaper (wsbridge bridge.rs:31,86) remains the backstop for flows that are really dead.
test_plan: New #[test]s in crates/holtburger-session/src/session/tests.rs (`server_silent_*`), run by the orchestrator with capped-build `cargo test -p holtburger-session server_silent`: (a) last_recv_time 20 s ago and previous check 5 s ago gives false; (b) last_recv_time 141 s ago and previous check 5 s ago gives true; (c) last_recv_time 200 s ago and previous check 200 s ago (client stalled) gives false on that tick and true on the next tick 5 s later; (d) a ScriptedTransport delivering only a TIME_SYNC packet advances session.last_recv_time. Live check (orchestrator, single tab, ?nosw=1): stay at character select for 150 s; no 'server-side session presumed dead' disconnect.
already_tracked: no (PARITY-STATUS net_session_protocol has no open items; the 90 s detector came from conn-fix 6d37513f, which soak-tested only in-world bots)

verify.reasons: Re-read lib.rs:44926-44945. The detector reads `last_recv_instant`, with `Some(t) => t.elapsed() > 90s, None => loop_started_at.elapsed() > 60s`. It runs before the InWorld/EnteringWorld gate, so it runs in every state, and the select! at 44880 has no `biased;`. rg confirms the only writer is session/messages/mod.rs:89. The SessionEvent::TimeSync arm (mod.rs:75-83) does `return LoopFlow::Continue` before that stamp. recv_message (receive.rs:403-461) returns an empty Vec for ACE's ack-only packets, so those never stamp it either. LoopState::Idle covers char select and chargen (lib.rs:41921-41935). ForceKeepalive (commands/lifecycle.rs:39-75) and the 5 s ping are both gated to InWorld/EnteringWorld, so at char select ACE sends no game messages. ACE sends only a TimeSync every 20 s and an ack-only packet every 2 s (ace-server NetworkSession.cs:31-32, 203-215). holtburger ACKs the TimeSync, which refreshes ACE's 60 s TimeoutTick (NetworkSession.cs:326-329), so ACE keeps the session while holtburger drops it after 90 s. That makes the char-select/chargen false disconnect real. Decomp verified: ClientNet::ProcessConnection (acclient.c:372842) tests `Timer::cur_time - lastDidUseTime_ < 140.0 && Timer::local_time - m_LocalTimeLastGotData > 140.0`. SharedNet::ProcessPacket (372105) stamps m_LocalTimeLastGotData for each accepted packet. SharedNet::UseTime (369884) writes lastDidUseTime_ after the read, and ClientNet::UseTime (370143) runs the connection pass first. OpenAC WorldSession.cs:382 (140.0) and IsServerSilent at 409-424 match, and the cited test names exist. Not tracked: PARITY-STATUS net_session_protocol has `open: []`. The detector came from 6d37513f, which soak-tested only in-world bots. I could NOT verify the ?netWorker freeze sub-claim. In Chrome, messages posted during a long main-thread task usually get an earlier enqueue order than delayed timer tasks, so the recv arm probably drains and stamps first. The freeze case is plausible but unproven.
verify.corrections: The proposed main fix has a flaw: it uses Session::last_recv_time. receive.rs:68 stamps that for every datagram, BEFORE checksum or ISAAC validation, and ACE's cleartext ack-only packets arrive every 2 s. With that as the liveness signal, a session whose S2C ISAAC stream is desynchronised (the net-3 failure: every encrypted packet fails silently) would never be reaped. Today the 90 s message-based detector is the only thing that reaps that state, because the bridge's ACE-silence reaper does not fire while ACE keeps sending. The proposed Proxy=>false plus a worker-side raw check has the same blind spot. Better fix: keep a decode-health signal and count TimeSync in it. TimeSync is encrypted and only produces an event if ISAAC validated, so it proves the stream is healthy and arrives every 20 s in every state. Add retail's stall guard on top. The netWorker-freeze part of the title is unverified.
verify.implementation_notes: 1) apps/holtburger-web/src/session/messages/mod.rs: move `*last_recv_instant.borrow_mut() = Some(web_time::Instant::now());` from after the `match event` to before `let bytes = match event {`, so SessionEvent::TimeSync also refreshes liveness. This covers both lanes, because the proxy forwards RX_KIND_TIMESYNC into the same handler. Side effect: the link-status indicator (lib.rs:35771 sessionLastRecvAgeMs) also counts TimeSync, which is fine. 2) lib.rs recv loop: next to `loop_started_at` (around 44772), add `let mut prev_keepalive_tick = web_time::Instant::now();` and a const SILENCE = 140 s (retail; it can stay 90 s if the owner prefers). In the keepalive arm: `let now = Instant::now(); let since_prev = now.saturating_duration_since(prev_keepalive_tick); prev_keepalive_tick = now;`. Evaluate inbound_dead only when `since_prev < SILENCE`, which is the lastDidUseTime_ guard. Keep the `None => 60 s` handshake branch. Update the log text to match the threshold. 3) Put the decision in a pure, non-wasm-gated helper so it can be unit-tested natively: e.g. `pub(crate) fn session_presumed_dead(last: Option<Instant>, loop_started: Instant, prev_tick: Instant, now: Instant, silence: Duration) -> bool` in a small module such as src/session_liveness.rs. #[cfg(test)] cases: last 20 s ago with prev tick 5 s ago gives false; last 141 s ago with prev 5 s gives true; last 200 s ago with prev 200 s (client stalled) gives false; None with loop started 61 s ago gives true. The orchestrator runs it once with capped-build `cargo test -p holtburger-web --lib session_presumed_dead`. 4) Do NOT switch to Session::last_recv_time unless the stamp moves after validate_received_packet_checksum AND net-3 lands first. 5) Optional escape `?netSilenceRetail=off`, parsed via flag_search() at recv-loop start like parse_retail_leash_flag (lib.rs:44712), restoring the old 90 s message-only check with no stall guard; add a url-flags.md row. 6) Orchestrator live check, single tab, ?nosw=1: idle at character select for 150 s with no 'presumed dead' disconnect; then in-world, kill ACE's flow and confirm a disconnect within threshold + 5 s.

title: A cleartext S2C RequestRetransmit packet (ACE reuses its current sequence) is ordered as data and can replace a lost data packet, which is then lost for good
decomp_evidence: SharedNet::ProcessNewSeqNum (acclient.c:372062): only ENCRYPTED packets (`header_ & 2`) that are not newer must match a NAKed id (372088-372092 `if (!(v2->m_Hdr.header_ & 2) || lhs_newer(...)) goto LABEL_10; v7 = AVL::Remove(&v3->m_SeqIDsWeNAKed, v4); if (!v7) return 0;`). SharedNet::ProcessNewestSeqNum (369054) treats a cleartext packet's sequence as BORROWED (369062 `if (!(pkt->m_Hdr.header_ & 2)) ++v2;`), so the id itself is NAKed and highestIDReceived_ moves but the id is never 'satisfied'. A cleartext packet therefore never consumes a data sequence.
openac_evidence: Transport/InboundSequenceTracker.cs:87 `uint end = encrypted ? sequence : unchecked(sequence + 1u);` NAKs a cleartext packet's own borrowed id, and cleartext admissions never satisfy a parked id. Pinned by tests/AcDream.Core.Net.Tests/Transport/InboundSequenceTrackerTests.cs `Cleartext_AtHighestPlusOne_NaksItsOwnBorrowedId` and `Cleartext_AtHighest_NoNak_NoKey_NoWatermarkChange`.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-session/src/session/receive.rs:217-220 `header.flags != packet_flags::ACK_SEQUENCE && (header.sequence != 0 || BLOB_FRAGMENTS)`. Only pure ACKs are excluded, so a NAK (flags = REQUEST_RETRANSMIT, sequence N) is ordered. At receive.rs:322 (`received_sequence != expected` is false when N == expected), finalize_ordered_server_packet runs (231-242): `self.last_server_seq = packet.header.sequence` and `self.queue_ack(packet.header.sequence)`. ACE stamps NAKs with CurrentValue, the last DATA sequence it sent (ace-server NetworkSession.cs:719 `bool isNak = ...RequestRetransmit`, :722-723 `if (Flags == AckSequence || isNak) Sequence = CurrentValue`). ACE applies the same rule to client NAKs, handling them before the reorder stage (:283-307 `return; //cleartext crc NAK is never accompanied by additional data`).
discrepancy: If data packet N is lost (e.g. kernel drop at the bridge) and ACE then sends a NAK (seq N, because of a C2S gap), holtburger treats the NAK as packet N. last_server_seq becomes N, N is ACKed (so ACE stops caching it), and the real N, if it ever arrives, is dropped as 'received again'. Its fragments (a CreateObject, a piece of a multi-fragment blob) are lost without any error. Retail and OpenAC never let a cleartext packet satisfy a sequence.
proposed_change: receive.rs:217 should_order_server_packet: also return false when `header.flags & packet_flags::REQUEST_RETRANSMIT != 0 && header.flags & packet_flags::ENCRYPTED_CHECKSUM == 0`. Keep ACE's cleartext RejectRetransmit ordered, because ACE gives it a fresh NextValue sequence (NetworkSession.cs:724-725). In finalize_ordered_server_packet (231-242), queue the ACK only when should_order_server_packet(&packet.header) is true, and pass `self.last_server_seq` (the cumulative watermark) instead of `packet.header.sequence`. Otherwise the now-unordered NAK would ACK its borrowed id and ACE would drop everything below N from its retransmit cache (NetworkSession.cs AcknowledgeSequence prunes `x < sequence`). Pair this with net-4 so the borrowed id is still used to detect the gap.
test_plan: New #[tokio::test] `test_cleartext_nak_does_not_consume_lost_data_sequence` in crates/holtburger-session/src/session/tests.rs, built with the existing ScriptedTransport and build_transport_packet helpers. Set last_server_seq=5 and has_server_seq=true. Inbound: a cleartext REQUEST_RETRANSMIT packet with sequence 6 (payload count=1 id=3), then build_single_fragment_packet(6, [AA,BB]). The first recv_message returns no events. The second returns Message([AA,BB]) and last_server_seq == 6. No sent ACK carries 6 before the data packet arrives. Today the second call errors with 'Empty' because packet 6 is dropped as a duplicate. Run with capped-build `cargo test -p holtburger-session cleartext_nak`.
already_tracked: no

verify.reasons: receive.rs:217-220 `should_order_server_packet` excludes only `flags == ACK_SEQUENCE`, so ACE's NAK (flags == 0x1000, cleartext) with sequence != 0 is ordered. When its sequence equals `expected` (receive.rs:322 branch), finalize_ordered_server_packet (231-242) sets `last_server_seq = seq` and calls queue_ack(seq). Any later real packet with that sequence is dropped as 'received again' (receive.rs:313-320). If it arrives first as out-of-order, buffer_out_of_order_packet uses `or_insert` (reliability.rs:84-86), so the NAK keeps the slot and the real packet loses. ACE verified: DoRequestForRetransmission builds `Header.Flags = PacketHeaderFlags.RequestRetransmit` with no EncryptedChecksum (NetworkSession.cs:418). FlushPackets stamps `if (Flags == AckSequence || isNak) Sequence = CurrentValue`, so the sequence is borrowed and the NAK is not cached (719-727). SendPacket draws ISAAC only when EncryptedChecksum is set. ACE handles client cleartext NAKs before its reorder stage (283-307). Decomp verified: SharedNet::ProcessNewSeqNum (acclient.c:372062) removes a NAKed id only for encrypted, not-newer packets. SharedNet::ProcessNewestSeqNum (369054) does `if (!(header_ & 2)) ++v2;`, so a cleartext packet's own id is NAKed and never satisfied. OpenAC InboundSequenceTracker.cs:87 `uint end = encrypted ? sequence : unchecked(sequence + 1u);` matches, and the cited tests exist. ACE's PacketAck prune `x < sequence` (NetworkSession.cs:669) confirms that ACKing a borrowed id also drops lower unacked ids from ACE's cache. The trigger (an ACE NAK, caused by a C2S gap, arriving just as S2C packet N is lost) is rare over WS to localhost UDP, but the corruption is silent when it happens.
verify.corrections: Severity MED is generous given how rare the trigger is (it needs C2S loss or reordering at ACE, coinciding with S2C loss), but the defect and the fix are exactly as described. The proposed fix is correct. Keeping ACE's cleartext RejectRetransmit ordered is right, because ACE gives it NextValue (FlushPackets). Related, not in this finding: S2C RejectRetransmit ids are only logged (receive.rs:149-156). Because holtburger delivers whole packets in order, a rejected id blocks the stream until the 180-request give-up. Retail SharedNet::HandleEmptyAck (acclient.c:372177) just removes the ids from the NAK set.
verify.implementation_notes: crates/holtburger-session/src/session/receive.rs: (1) In should_order_server_packet, add an early `if header.flags & packet_flags::REQUEST_RETRANSMIT != 0 && header.flags & packet_flags::ENCRYPTED_CHECKSUM == 0 { return false; }`. Keep the existing pure-ACK rule. Do NOT exclude REJECT_RETRANSMIT, since ACE sequences it with NextValue. (2) In finalize_ordered_server_packet, move the ACK inside the ordered branch: `if self.should_order_server_packet(&packet.header) { self.last_server_seq = ...; self.has_server_seq = true; self.retransmit_requests_since_progress = 0; self.queue_ack(self.last_server_seq)?; }`. Delete the separate `packet.header.sequence > 0 && flags != ACK_SEQUENCE` ACK so a borrowed id is never ACKed (ACE prunes `< seq`). Ordered packets behave exactly as before because last_server_seq == packet seq. (3) The processing in process_received_packet_metadata, which retransmits the C2S ids the NAK lists, is unchanged. New #[tokio::test] `test_cleartext_nak_does_not_consume_lost_data_sequence` in crates/holtburger-session/src/session/tests.rs: Session::new_test(), last_server_seq=5, has_server_seq=true. ScriptedTransport inbound is [build_transport_packet(PacketHeader{sequence:6, flags:REQUEST_RETRANSMIT, size:8,..}, &[1u32 LE, 3u32 LE]), build_single_fragment_packet(6, &[0xAA,0xBB])]. The first recv_message gives Ok(empty) and last_server_seq is still 5. The second gives an event Message([AA,BB]) and last_server_seq == 6. No ACK_SEQUENCE packet sent before the data carries payload 6. A sibling case: last_server_seq=4, NAK seq 6, then data 5, then data 6, and both data messages are delivered. Existing tests test_request_retransmit_sends_cached_packet and test_retransmit_uses_cached_packet_with_piggybacked_ack use recv_packet and are unaffected; test_piggybacked_ack_still_queues_ack_for_ordered_packet must still pass. The orchestrator runs it with capped-build `cargo test -p holtburger-session cleartext_nak`. No URL flag is needed (protocol correctness in a shared crate). Needs a wasm rebuild.

title: ISAAC key search and reorder window are limited to 256: losing more than 256 server packets in a burst silently breaks decryption and the session dies
decomp_evidence: Retail does not search for keys. It parks one key per missing sequence: SharedNet::ProcessNewestSeqNum (369054) calls ReceiverData::AddNakked for every id between highestIDReceived_+1 and the new id, and AddNakked (376642) draws `CryptoSystem::GetNextCryptoSeed(this->cryptoIncoming_, v4)` (376676) and stores it per id. ProcessNewSeqNum (372090) removes the parked key when the late or retransmitted packet arrives and decrypts with it (372099). The only limits are SeqIDSanityCheck (371343): the packet is dropped (not disconnected) if seq > highest+0x7FFF or the NAK set exceeds 0x9C40 (371368).
openac_evidence: Transport/InboundSequenceTracker.cs implements the retail model: SanityWindow = 0x7FFF (:10); Admit (:61-104) parks a drawn word per missing id (AddNakked :181), consumes the parked word for not-newer encrypted packets, and drops encrypted duplicates before touching the keystream (:76 `if (!_nakSet.Remove(sequence, out ParkedWord parked))`). OnCleartextRejectSequence (:142) handles ACE's cleartext RejectRetransmit, which takes a sequence without an ISAAC word. Pinned by InboundSequenceTrackerTests `GapWalk_ParksTheMissingKey_LaterPacketsAndLateArrivalDecode`, `SanityWindow_HighestPlus0x7FFF_Accepted_OnePastIt_Dropped` and `S2CLoss_LaterPacketsStillDecode_LateRedeliveryCompletesTheMessage`.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-protocol/src/crypto.rs:42 `MAXIMUM_EFFORT_LEVEL: usize = 256`; search (:73-93) walks at most `256 - xors.len()` words. After one failed walk xors is full, so effort is 0 and every later key fails. receive.rs:193-197 drops packets whose key is not found (`continue`) before any gap logic, so no retransmit is ever requested. types.rs:45 `MAX_RETRANSMIT_SEQUENCE_WINDOW: u32 = 256`. reliability.rs:74 drops buffered packets more than 256 ahead, and :187-195 returns Err ('Abnormal server packet sequence', which disconnects the session) when the gap exceeds 257. The loss is real: wsbridge bridge.rs:412-414 says a stalled browser reader 'silently dropp[ed] ACE→client datagrams in the kernel', and the bridge UDP socket (bridge.rs:196) never raises SO_RCVBUF, unlike native Session::new (session/api.rs:9,22, 2 MB).
discrepancy: Retail and OpenAC survive gaps up to 0x7FFF sequences because keys are tied to sequence numbers. holtburger's search-based recovery has a hard 256-packet limit. In direct (default) mode, a browser main-thread stall during a load burst makes the bridge stop reading UDP. If more than 256 server packets are dropped in the kernel, the S2C keystream is permanently out of step: every encrypted packet fails its checksum without an error, nothing is NAKed, and the session freezes until the 90 s detector disconnects it. A gap of exactly 257 hits the Err path and disconnects immediately.
proposed_change: Small mitigation (S/M): raise crypto.rs MAXIMUM_EFFORT_LEVEL and types.rs MAX_RETRANSMIT_SEQUENCE_WINDOW together (e.g. 4096; MAX_PENDING_SERVER_PACKETS follows). In reliability.rs:187-195, replace the Err with a logged drop of the over-window packet, like retail SeqIDSanityCheck, which never disconnects. send_request_retransmit already caps the list at the lowest 115 ids, and the net-4 timer re-NAKs the rest. In apps/holtburger-wsbridge/src/bridge.rs:196, set SockRef::from(&udp).set_recv_buffer_size(2 MiB) as Session::new does. Full fix (L): port OpenAC's InboundSequenceTracker into holtburger-session, replacing Isaac::search on the S2C path: a BTreeMap<u32 seq, u32 key> of parked words drawn in order as gaps appear; not-newer encrypted packets must hit the map, otherwise drop before validation (duplicates cost no keystream); re-park on checksum failure; remove on RejectRetransmit; reclaim words for ACE's cleartext RejectRetransmit 'bubble'.

verify.reasons: crypto.rs:42 `MAXIMUM_EFFORT_LEVEL: usize = 256`. search() (73-93) checks current_key, then xors, then walks `256 - xors.len()` words, inserting each into xors. A failed walk leaves xors full and current_key advanced, so effort is 0 for every later key. Worked through: with xors empty, a loss of k consecutive encrypted packets is recoverable iff k <= 256. At k >= 257 the next key is not found and the stream is dead. receive.rs:162-205 returns Ok(false) on a search miss, and receive.rs:299-301/351-353 `continue` before any gap or NAK logic, so nothing is ever requested. ACE's 2 s cleartext acks pass but are non-ordered, and its TimeSyncs are encrypted and fail. In-world the session freezes until the 90 s detector fires. types.rs:45 sets the window to 256; MAX_PENDING_SERVER_PACKETS = window + 2 (types.rs:28). The reliability.rs:74 drop and the reliability.rs:187-195 Err are as cited. Decomp verified: ReceiverData::AddNakked (376642) does `seqNum = CryptoSystem::GetNextCryptoSeed(...)` and AVL::Add per id. SeqIDSanityCheck (371343) uses highest+0x7FFF and `m_SeqIDsWeNAKed._currNum <= 0x9C40`, and drops rather than disconnects (ProcessNewSeqNum returns 0). OpenAC InboundSequenceTracker.cs:10 SanityWindow=0x7FFF and Admit at 61-104 match. Bridge: UdpSocket::bind with no SO_RCVBUF (bridge.rs:196), whereas native Session::new sets 2 MiB via socket2 (api.rs:9,22). The bridge comment at bridge.rs:412-414 documents kernel drops while the WS send was parked. Not tracked.
verify.corrections: (1) The claim that 'a gap of exactly 257 hits the Err path and disconnects immediately' is wrong. With xors empty, 257 lost packets fail the key search (which reaches at most 256 words), so the next packet is dropped silently and never reaches send_request_retransmit. Even after an earlier duplicate walk fills xors, the reach stays 256 from the last consumed key. The Err at reliability.rs:187 is reachable only when the sequence gap exceeds the key gap, i.e. when ACE's cleartext RejectRetransmit 'bubbles' (NextValue, no ISAAC word) fall inside the gap. (2) The trigger is narrower than implied. Since conn-fix, WS_SEND_TIMEOUT=15 s (bridge.rs:37) tears the flow down after a 15 s stall, so the dead-keystream case needs more than 256 drops (plus whatever the kernel buffers) within a stall shorter than 15 s. That is plausible during a CreateObject flood, but it is unmeasured. (3) set_recv_buffer_size(2 MiB) is silently clamped to net.core.rmem_max (~208 KB by default on Linux) unless the bridge host raises it, so the bridge mitigation is partial. (4) A hazard the fix must not widen: a packet that passes validation consumes its key (consume_key_value). If it is then discarded (window drop at reliability.rs:74, or highest-eviction), a later retransmission can never validate. Keep the sequence window >= the effort level plus some slack.
verify.implementation_notes: Mitigation only; the full InboundSequenceTracker port is L effort and should be a separate, reviewed change. (a) crates/holtburger-protocol/src/crypto.rs: raise MAXIMUM_EFFORT_LEVEL to 4096. A duplicate or forged packet walks at most 4096 ISAAC words plus HashSet inserts, well under 1 ms, and xors holds at most 4096 u32. (b) crates/holtburger-session/src/session/types.rs: set MAX_RETRANSMIT_SEQUENCE_WINDOW = 4096 + 64, deliberately larger than the effort level so the bubble slack never discards an already-validated packet. MAX_PENDING_SERVER_PACKETS follows automatically (about 4 K entries of at most 1 KB each, worst case about 4 MB; acceptable, or cap it separately at 1024 and evict the highest as today). (c) reliability.rs send_request_retransmit: when `missing_span > MAX_RETRANSMIT_SEQUENCE_WINDOW + 1`, log::warn and return Ok(()) without sending, instead of Err (retail SeqIDSanityCheck drops, never disconnects). Keep the Err only for the `!is_newer_u32` case, or make that a drop too. (d) apps/holtburger-wsbridge: add `socket2 = { workspace = true }` (workspace Cargo.toml:53 already pins 0.6) and, after `UdpSocket::bind` at bridge.rs:196, call `socket2::SockRef::from(&*udp_or_socket).set_recv_buffer_size(2 * 1024 * 1024)`, logging (not failing) on error, mirroring session/api.rs:22. Keep test_isaac_search_handles_out_of_order_keys passing. In session/tests.rs add `test_gap_wider_than_window_is_dropped_not_fatal`: call session.send_request_retransmit(last_server_seq + 1 + MAX_RETRANSMIT_SEQUENCE_WINDOW + 10) directly with has_server_seq=true and assert Ok with no REQUEST_RETRANSMIT sent. A packet-driven test needs a valid ISAAC checksum; build_transport_packet makes cleartext packets, so call the fn directly. The existing test_send_request_retransmit_wraps_sequence_window must still pass. title: Lost last packet of a burst is detected only by the next encrypted packet, and lost-packet requests are not re-sent on a timer (retail: cleartext sequence used as a hint, re-request every 0.6 s)
decomp_evidence: SharedNet::ProcessNewestSeqNum (369054/369062): any cleartext packet newer than highestIDReceived_ NAKs every id up to AND INCLUDING its borrowed sequence. ACE's 2 s ack-only packets carry its current sequence, so a lost last packet is noticed within 2 s. ClientNet::ProcessConnection runs every net pump and calls SharedNet::EnqueueNaks while the NAK set is non-empty (372894-372898); otherwise it calls EnqueuePak. EnqueueNaks is gated by `timeStamp_ > 0.6` (371458) and sends up to 114 ids (ReceiverData::GetNaks 376487 caps at 0x72). EnqueuePak is gated by `>= 2.0` (371414) and shares the same timestamp.
openac_evidence: Transport/AckNakScheduler.cs:8-12 `AckGateSeconds = 2.0`, `NakGateSeconds = 0.6`, `MaxNakIdsPerPacket = 114`. Sweep (:54-71) re-emits RequestRetransmit on the 0.6 s gate whenever NakCount > 0, independent of new arrivals. It is driven every tick by ReliableTransport.Sweep (Transport/ReliableTransport.cs) via WorldSession.cs:829. Pinned by tests/.../Transport/NakEmissionTests.cs `NakGate_ClosedAtExactly600ms_OpensJustPastIt` and `LongLoss_NaksOnTheGateCadence_NoAcks_GapHealsInsideTheWindow`.
holt_evidence: receive.rs:306-309 and 359-362: non-ordered packets (ACE's ack-only packets, flags == ACK_SEQUENCE, seq = CurrentValue per ace-server NetworkSession.cs:722-723) go straight to finalize with no gap check. NAKs are sent only from the out-of-order branch (receive.rs:336-338 and 389-391) when a NEWER encrypted packet arrives, gated by `REQUEST_RETRANSMIT_INTERVAL = 1s` (types.rs:46; reliability.rs:246-253). Nothing re-NAKs on a timer, so a lost retransmission is re-requested only if another out-of-order packet arrives at least 1 s later.
discrepancy: If the last data packet before a quiet period is lost, holtburger does not notice until the next encrypted packet arrives: up to about 20 s at character select (ACE TimeSync cadence) and about 5 s in-world (ping responses). Retail notices within about 2.6 s (next ACE ack plus the 0.6 s NAK gate). A lost retransmission stays a hole until unrelated traffic happens to arrive, while every later message waits in pending_server_packets.
proposed_change: (a) Gap hint: in both non-ordered branches of recv_ordered_packet (receive.rs:306 and :359), before finalize, if `self.has_server_seq && seq != 0 && flags & ENCRYPTED_CHECKSUM == 0 && is_newer_u32(seq, self.last_server_seq)`, then `if self.should_request_retransmit(expected, seq.wrapping_add(1)) { self.send_request_retransmit(seq.wrapping_add(1))?; }`. Passing seq+1 makes the existing [desired, received) builder include the borrowed id, as retail's `++v2` does. (b) Timer-driven re-NAK: add `highest_server_seq_seen` (retail highestIDReceived_), updated on buffering and gap hints. When it is newer than last_server_seq, include `last_request_retransmit_time + 600ms` among the wake deadlines in recv_ordered_packet's select (receive.rs:264-291, alongside next_pending_control_deadline), and on expiry call send_request_retransmit(highest_server_seq_seen + 1). Change REQUEST_RETRANSMIT_INTERVAL to 600 ms (retail and OpenAC). Optionally cap the list at 114 (retail GetNaks). Rescale RETRANSMIT_GIVE_UP_REQUESTS (180 at 1 Hz becomes 300 at 0.6 s) or make it time-based, so the give-up stays at about 3 min.

(2) `test_pending_gap_renaks_on_timer`: buffer seq 8 with last_server_seq=5, set last_request_retransmit_time to now-700ms, drive the new timer path, and assert a second REQUEST_RETRANSMIT listing [6,7]. (3) The existing test_out_of_order_server_packet_requests_retransmit and test_first_server_packet_sequence_two_does_not_request_retransmit still pass. Run with capped-build `cargo test -p holtburger-session retransmit`.

verify.reasons: In holtburger receive.rs (non-ordered branches at ~306-309 and ~359-362), packets that should_order_server_packet rejects (ACE's pure AckSequence) go straight to finalize with no comparison against last_server_seq. RequestRetransmit is sent only from the out-of-order branches when a newer ordered packet arrives, gated by should_request_retransmit with REQUEST_RETRANSMIT_INTERVAL = 1 s (types.rs:46; reliability.rs:245-253). Nothing re-NAKs on a timer: recv_ordered_packet's only timer is next_pending_control_deadline, which tracks queued control packets. ACE verified: the ack-only bundle is cleartext (EncryptedChecksum is set only for messages or TimeSync), its flags are exactly AckSequence and its Sequence is CurrentValue (NetworkSession.cs:722-723, 834-835, 922-929), sent every 2 s (203-215). Decomp verified: ProcessNewestSeqNum (acclient.c:369054) NAKs through the borrowed id for cleartext packets. ClientNet::ProcessConnection (372894-372898) calls EnqueueNaks every pump while the NAK set is non-empty. EnqueueNaks is gated `> 0.6` (371447 block) and EnqueuePak `>= 2.0` (371404 block), sharing timeStamp_. GetNaks caps at 0x72/114 (376487). OpenAC AckNakScheduler.cs:8-12 and Sweep at 54-71 match, and the cited NakEmissionTests exist. Practical impact is modest: in-world, ACE traffic is near-continuous, and at char select the next 20 s TimeSync arrives out of order and triggers the NAK. Still a real retail divergence.
verify.corrections: Part (a) as written can disconnect the session. send_request_retransmit returns Err when `missing_span > MAX_RETRANSMIT_SEQUENCE_WINDOW + 1` (reliability.rs:187-195), and recv_message propagates it. A gap hint from a cleartext ack whose sequence is far ahead (e.g. after the net-3 burst) would then kill the session. The hint path must skip, or clamp to the window, instead of erroring; better, land net-3(c) first. In (b), once a 0.6 s cadence lands, rescale RETRANSMIT_GIVE_UP_REQUESTS from 180 to 300, or make it time-based (about 180 s); otherwise the give-up drops to about 108 s. After net-2 lands, ACE's cleartext NAK is also non-ordered and should feed the same hint.

Passing s+1 makes the [desired, received) builder include the borrowed id s, as retail's `++v2` does. The builder already skips ids present in pending_server_packets. (b) Add `highest_server_seq_seen: u32` to Session (types.rs, initialised in api.rs). Update it in buffer_out_of_order_packet and the hint. While `is_newer_u32(highest_server_seq_seen, last_server_seq)`, compute `nak_deadline = last_request_retransmit_time.unwrap_or(now) + REQUEST_RETRANSMIT_INTERVAL` and use `min(control_deadline, nak_deadline)` as the select timer in recv_ordered_packet. Keep the parser limit for inbound lists at 115, since ACE sends up to 115. Make sure the timer only arms when a gap exists, so an idle session does not busy-wake. title: Reply to a server EchoRequest reuses the server's packet header (its sequence and id), encrypts it and caches it under that sequence; retail adds an EchoResponse optional header to the next outgoing packet
decomp_evidence: SharedNet::ProcessOptionalHeader (acclient.c:370711): mask 0x2000000 (EchoRequest) produces `CEchoResponseHeader::CreateFromData(*(float *)&pHdr[1].vfptr)` (370753), queued with PacketController::EnqueueOptionalHeader. It is an optional header on the next outgoing packet, with the echoed time; no new packet and no reused sequence.
openac_evidence: OpenAC parses S2C EchoRequestClientTime (Packets/PacketHeaderOptional.cs:113-116) and never sends a packet in reply, so no sequence or ISAAC word is spent (rg for EchoRequest/EchoResponse in WorldSession.cs and Transport/*.cs finds no emitter).
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-session/src/session/receive.rs:244-248 `let mut resp = packet.header.clone(); resp.flags = packet_flags::ECHO_RESPONSE; self.queue_packet_to_addr(resp, &[], ...)`. build_packet_bytes (send.rs:69-119) then adds ACK_SEQUENCE and ENCRYPTED_CHECKSUM, consuming a C2S ISAAC word, and flush_pending_control_packets (send.rs:231-234) runs maybe_cache_packet under the SERVER's sequence via `or_insert`. The payload is empty, although ECHO_RESPONSE is 8 bytes (transport.rs ECHO_RESPONSE_SIZE = 8).
discrepancy: Latent today: vanilla ACE only sends EchoResponse, never EchoRequest (ace-server NetworkSession.cs:939-946). If the handler ever fires, it sends a malformed packet with the server's id and sequence, uses up a C2S ISAAC word that ACE will never match, and can put a bogus entry in the C2S retransmit cache under a sequence a later real packet will use. A later ACE retransmit request would then resend the echo instead of the data.
proposed_change: Delete the ECHO_REQUEST block in finalize_ordered_server_packet (OpenAC behaviour; ACE never sends one). Alternatively, for retail fidelity, store the echoed f32 and write an ECHO_RESPONSE optional header (client_time f32 + holding_time f32, in optional-header flag order) in build_packet_bytes on the next outgoing data packet, without a new sequence or a cache entry.
test_plan: New #[tokio::test] `test_server_echo_request_does_not_emit_packet_with_server_sequence` in crates/holtburger-session/src/session/tests.rs: inbound packet seq 2 with ECHO_REQUEST and a 4-byte f32. After recv_message and flush_pending_control_packets, assert no sent packet has header.sequence == 2 with the ECHO_RESPONSE flag, and cached_packets has no entry created by it. Run with capped-build `cargo test -p holtburger-session echo_request`.

verify.reasons: receive.rs:244-248: `let mut resp = packet.header.clone(); resp.flags = packet_flags::ECHO_RESPONSE; self.queue_packet_to_addr(resp, &[], self.server_addr, Instant::now())?;`. queue_packet_to_addr calls build_packet_bytes (send.rs:69-119), which adds ACK_SEQUENCE when has_server_seq and ENCRYPTED_CHECKSUM when isaac_c2s exists, and consumes a C2S ISAAC word (`isaac.consume_key()`). The header keeps the server's sequence and id. The payload omits the 8-byte echo body (transport.rs:27 ECHO_RESPONSE_SIZE = 8); calculate_payload_hash does not error, it just hashes the truncated optional region, so a malformed packet goes out. flush_pending_control_packets (send.rs:203-235) then calls maybe_cache_packet, which caches it under the server's sequence when that is >= 2 (reliability.rs:16-37, or_insert). Decomp verified: SharedNet::ProcessOptionalHeader (acclient.c:370711) handles mask 0x2000000 with CEchoResponseHeader::CreateFromData(float) plus PacketController::EnqueueOptionalHeader, i.e. an optional header on a later packet, not a new packet. ACE never sends an S2C EchoRequest: its only EchoRequest handling is inbound (NetworkSession.cs:439-443), and it emits only EchoResponse (943). holtburger never sends a C2S EchoRequest (rg finds no emitter), so the handler is latent.
verify.corrections: None of substance. Deleting the block is the correct minimal fix for an ACE-only client. The retail-fidelity alternative (an EchoResponse optional header on the next outgoing packet) has no consumer and is not worth building now.

title: AutonomousPosition is sent while airborne and the in-window check uses a contact byte, not retail's contact-plane compare
decomp_evidence: CommandInterpreter::SendPositionEvent (acclient.c:718202): the pack is built only `if ( v3 & 1 ) { if ( v3 & 2 )` (transient_state CONTACT && ON_WALKABLE, :718225/:718227) and Position::IsValid; on emit it stamps last_sent_position_time, last_sent_position and last_sent_contact_plane (:718242-718245). The AP contact byte is therefore always 1. When the player is airborne the call is a no-op and stamps nothing, so the first grounded frame sends. ShouldSendPositionEvent (:718108-718138): when time_between_position_events (1.0) + last_sent_position_time < now it sends on `objcell_id != last || !Frame::is_equal`. Otherwise it sends on cell change or `Plane::operator==(&last_sent_contact_plane, &player->contact_plane) == 0` (:718131). Plane::operator== (:717723) uses |dN_i| <= 0.0002 and |dd| < 0.0002. Frame::is_equal (:96700) uses a 0.0002 per-component tolerance on origin and quaternion, not a bit-exact compare. The ctor (:717760-717778) sets last_sent_position.objcell_id = 0, so the first grounded UseTime sends at once. SmartBox::UseTime (:146256) runs physics, then net blobs, then cmdinterp UseTime every frame.
openac_evidence: LocalPlayerOutboundController.cs:95-102 returns early unless `controller.ShouldSendPositionEvent(position, controller.ContactPlane, ...)` and `controller.CanSendPositionEvent`. PlayerMovementController.cs:1177 has `CanSendPositionEvent => _body.InContact && _body.OnWalkable`. :1279-1297 is the window split with ApproxPlaneEqual and ApproxFrameEqual (:2145-2165, epsilon 0.000199999995). The tests PlayerOutboundPositionTests.cs PositionEvent_CellOrContactPlaneChangeIsDueInsideInterval, PositionEvent_RetailPlaneDistanceBoundaryIsStrict and PositionEvent_FirstFrameIsDue pin this behaviour.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/system.rs:9252: the in-window branch is `if self.last_sent_autonomous_contact != Some(pulse.last_contact) { return true; }`, a 1-to-0 contact flip, so an AP fires the tick a jump or fall starts. The past-window branch keeps sending mid-air every 1 s. common.rs:127 `metadata.contact.unwrap_or(!world.player.is_airborne)` and :194 `last_contact: encode_last_contact(...)` send last_contact=0 APs. Nothing in maybe_send_autonomous_position_heartbeat (system.rs:9267-9345) or send_autonomous_position_sync (:9347) checks is_airborne. system.rs:9218-9224: when there is no prior send it `return past_window;`, and :9294-9296 arms a 1 s settle window before the first AP. system.rs:419-423 says "Retail's `Frame::is_equal` is a bit-exact compare" and uses AUTONOMOUS_POSE_EPSILON_M = 0.05. The retail-faithful gate already exists at command_interpreter.rs:872-921, but its seams are stubbed: system.rs:9518 `cur_time` returns 0.0, :9637 `player_position_event_ready` returns false, :9711 `send_autonomous_position` returns false. world.player.last_contact_plane (holtburger-world player/types.rs:1683, world-frame under USE_RETAIL_GROUND=true) is available but unused by the heartbeat.
discrepancy: Retail never sends an AutonomousPosition unless the player has contact and is on a walkable surface, and every AP it sends has last_contact=1. In-window it re-sends when the contact plane changes, for example when stepping onto a new terrain triangle or a floor. holtburger sends an AP the moment the player leaves the ground, then one every second mid-air with last_contact=0. It never re-sends on a grounded plane change. ACE answers every AP with SetRequestedLocation(position) and broadcasts it (Player_Tick.cs:513), so observers get mid-arc UpdatePositions that a retail client never produces, and ACE's LastContact flips false (GameActionAutonomousPosition.cs:26-30). holtburger's first AP is also delayed 1 s where retail sends it on the first grounded frame.
proposed_change: Minimal (M), in system.rs. (1) In maybe_send_autonomous_position_heartbeat and send_autonomous_position_sync, return Ok(false) without stamping anything when `world.player.is_airborne` (retail SendPositionEvent guard, :718225-718227). The first grounded tick then sends because last_sent_* are unchanged. (2) Replace `last_sent_autonomous_contact: Option<u8>` with `last_sent_contact_plane: Option<Plane>`, filled from `world.player.last_contact_plane.map(|(p, _)| p)` in note_autonomous_position_sent (pass world in). In autonomous_pose_changed's in-window branch, send when both planes are Some and differ by the retail Plane::operator== rule (|dN.x|,|dN.y|,|dN.z| <= 2e-4 and |dd| < 2e-4). A None plane is already covered by guard (1). (3) With no prior send, return true on any branch (retail compares cell 0 against the real cell). Arm the window on the first tick but still evaluate that tick. (4) Fix the system.rs:419-422 doc comment to cite the 0.0002 epsilons. title: RawMotionState pack writes the header from `flags` but bodies from Option presence, and never omits retail defaults
decomp_evidence: RawMotionState::Pack (acclient.c:332970) derives every flag bit from the field value at pack time. It omits current_holdkey == 1 (HoldKey_None), current_style == 0x8000003D, forward_command == 0x41000003, any hold key == 0, and any speed == 1.0f. It then writes exactly the flagged fields, so the header and body cannot disagree. Keyboard axis hold keys are 0 (Invalid) because MovementParameters' default bitfield 0x1EE0F includes 0x800 and ApplyMotion stores holdkey 0 (:332852). A retail W+Run MoveToState is therefore flags 0x5 (CURRENT_HOLD_KEY=2, FORWARD_COMMAND).
openac_evidence: RawMotionStatePacker.cs:23-46 computes flags by comparing each field with RawMotionState.Default, then writes only flagged fields. OpenAC's per-action loop writes 4 bytes without the speed float, which is an OpenAC bug; holtburger's 8-byte MotionItem is correct.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-protocol/src/messages/movement/types.rs:535 `let mut packed_flags = self.flags.bits() & 0x7FF;` then :539-571 `if let Some(val) = self.current_hold_key {...}` and so on. Bodies follow Option presence, not the header bits. common.rs:466-471 always sets CURRENT_HOLD_KEY, even for None (1). :483-493 and :496-506 always add FORWARD_HOLD_KEY|FORWARD_SPEED (1.0) and the sidestep equivalents. raw_motion_state_with_motion_style (common.rs:83-103) always sets CURRENT_STYLE under PreserveServer, including NonCombat.
discrepancy: A builder that sets an Option without its flag, or the reverse, emits a header that does not match the body. ACE then misparses the Position and sequence quartet after it, producing a silent bad MoveToState. Every MoveToState also carries 4-12 bytes that retail omits. Those bytes are semantically neutral on ACE, whose SetState defaults are in Physics/Animation/RawMotionState.cs:117-140.
proposed_change: In RawMotionState::pack, compute the header bits from Option presence. Take each bit from field.is_some(), keep the command count in bits 11-15, and debug_assert that the result equals self.flags & 0x7FF. Optionally, in the two common.rs builders, canonicalize to retail defaults. That means leaving current_hold_key unset when it is None(1), current_style unset for NonCombat, speeds unset at 1.0, and keyboard axis hold keys unset (Invalid; ACE adjust_motion falls back to CurrentHoldKey). This is byte parity with the real retail client, which ACE already accepts.

title: RP6 cull breaks emitter lifecycle: persistent emitters age out while culled and regrow on re-entry, and count-bounded emitters stop emitting

For a persistent emitter (!total_particles && total_seconds==0) it sets `v1->particles[v9].birthtime = PhysicsTimer::curr_time` for every slot (:331175), which freezes ages with no catch-up. For a finite emitter it ages and kills particles from birthtime and still runs `if ( ParticleEmitter::ShouldEmitParticle(v1) ) ParticleEmitter::RecordParticleEmission(v1);` (:331161-331162), so total_emitted and last_emit_time advance on schedule and StopEmitter fires on time. Retail never frustum-culls particle simulation; this distance degrade is its only culling.

Infinite emitters do `em.FrozenTime += dt` (:979), which EffectiveParticleAge (:1088) subtracts. Finite emitters age, kill, and emit virtually (`em.TotalEmitted++`, :1005). Pinned by tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Vfx/ParticleSystemTests.cs:652 InfiniteEmitter_DegradedTimeFreezesParticleAgeWithoutCatchUp and :1144 FiniteEmitter_DegradedDueEmissionRecordsBothRetailCounters.
holt_evidence: In the culled branch (particle_manager.js:1805-1883), a non-stopped emitter only gets `stopEmitter()` before `continue`, so updateParticles is skipped. Re-entry (:1800-1801) only calls `_setPartsVisible(emitter, true)`. The persistent update in particle.js:443-447 is `const elapsed = now - this.lastUpdateTime; ... this.lifetime += elapsed;`, and lastUpdateTime still holds the pre-cull time, so the first update after re-entry adds the whole off-screen interval and killParticle retires every particle. For count-bounded emitters totalEmitted is frozen while culled; the only workaround is a force-stop after `culledStopSeconds: 30` (:166, :1855-1859). The existing test (test_particle_rp6_cull_authority.mjs) uses lifespan 1000, so it cannot see this.
discrepancy: Look away from chimney smoke or fountain mist for longer than one lifespan and look back: the emitter is empty and refills over about one lifespan, at one emit per tick. Retail shows steady state, either fully simulated in range or frozen when degraded. A count-bounded one-shot culled mid-emission resumes emitting its remainder late when it re-enters the frustum, or is force-stopped at 30 s.
proposed_change: (a) Persistent (0/0) emitters, at zero per-tick cost. In the recheck block, when `nowCulled && !wasCulled`, stamp `emitter._rp6CulledAt = currentTime()`. On re-entry (:1800), compute `dt = now - emitter._rp6CulledAt` and for each `i < emitter._createdSlots` with `emitter.parts[i] !== null` apply `particles[i].lastUpdateTime += dt; particles[i].birthtime += dt`. This matches retail's birthtime reset and OpenAC's FrozenTime. (b) Finite emitters (totalParticles>0 || totalSeconds>0) that are not stopped: while culled, call `emitter.updateParticles()`, as the stopped-drain path already does, then re-hide with `_setPartsVisible(emitter,false)`. These are short-lived cast and one-shot emitters, so the cost is bounded, and emission, kill and stop stay on the retail schedule. With (b) in place, delete the `culledStopSeconds` force-stop. A cheaper alternative to (b) is retail-style virtual emission (`totalEmitted++`, `lastEmitTime`, `lastEmitOffset`) without numParticles++, which avoids the retail num_particles inflation that OpenAC deliberately reproduces.

title: Owner registry never learns that an emitter finished naturally: scoped handles stay bound, so a later CreateBlockingParticle on that handle is refused forever and owner id maps grow without bound
decomp_evidence: ParticleManager::UpdateParticles (acclient.c:329516-329520) removes a finished emitter from the object's particle_table: `if ( !ParticleEmitter::UpdateParticles(...) ) { LongNIHash::remove(v5, *v4); ParticleEmitter::~ParticleEmitter }`. ParticleManager::CreateBlockingParticleEmitter (:329528-329565) refuses only when the table lookup finds a live entry (`if ( v6->data ) return 0;`), so once the old emitter is gone the same id can be created again.
openac_evidence: ParticleHookSink subscribes to ParticleSystem.EmitterDied (src/AcDream.Core/Vfx/ParticleHookSink.cs:35). OnEmitterDied (:49-69) removes the (owner, logicalId) mapping and the per-entity handle. Pinned by tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Vfx/ParticleHookSinkTests.cs:227 NaturalRetirement_PrunesLogicalIdForBlockingReuse.
holt_evidence: owner_registry.js:205-210 `const existing = rec.scoped.get(handle); if (existing !== undefined) { if (blocking) { ... return 0; }`. At :271-273 it runs `rec.ids.set(id, manager); ... rec.scoped.set(handle, id);`. Only _destroyUnderlying and destroyAllForOwner ever remove these entries. ParticleManager's tick auto-removal (particle_manager.js:1887 `removeIds.push(id)`, then :1931 `this.particleTable.delete(id)`) notifies nobody. Entity hooks pass explicit handles plus blocking through this registry (on by default): entities.js:16993 `emitterId: emitterIdSeed,` and :16997 `await ownerRegistry.addEmitter(inst.guid >>> 0, ...)`. url-flags.md:1149 names the affected content: a looping script that re-fires a CreateBlockingParticle hook ('forge embers / a lantern').
discrepancy: After a finite emitter created with handle H drains naturally, every later CreateBlockingParticle(26) with H on that entity returns 0 for the rest of the entity's life. The effect plays once and never again, whereas retail re-creates it on the next loop iteration. Separately, `rec.ids` keeps one dead id for every naturally finished emitter (every animation-hook emitter on the long-lived local player). The map grows for the whole session and inflates emitterCountForOwner.
proposed_change: Add an optional retirement hook on ParticleManager, e.g. `this.onEmitterRemoved = null`, invoked with the id inside tick()'s removeIds loop and in destroyParticleEmitter. In ownerRegistry.addEmitter, install it once per manager (e.g. `manager.onEmitterRemoved ??= (id) => this._onRetired(manager, id)`) and keep a reverse map from underlying id to ownerKey. `_onRetired` deletes the id from `rec.ids`, removes any `rec.scoped` alias whose value === id, then calls `_pruneOwner`. The manager-level blocking check (particle_manager.js:1308) is already correct and needs no change.
test_plan: Extend test_particle_owner.mjs. Create a blocking emitter with handle 9 on owner 7 using a finite emitter (totalParticles 1, short lifespan) on a real ParticleManager with mocked time. Tick until it auto-removes, then assert `await reg.addEmitter(7, mgr, {emitterId: 9, blocking: true})` returns non-zero. title: Wire PlayScript (0xF755) hooks skip the object's ScriptManager: they run on wall-clock setTimeout with no back-to-back chaining
decomp_evidence: SmartBox::HandlePlayScriptType (acclient.c:143374-143390) calls CPhysicsObj::play_script(PScriptType, mod) (:320326-320348). That calls PhysicsScriptTable::GetScript, then play_script_internal (:318035-318066), then ScriptManager::AddScript on the object's single script_manager. AddScriptInternal (:329069-329121) starts a new script at `v4->script->length + v4->start_time` of last_data whenever something is queued. title: Next Monster and Previous Monster are swapped, and the cycle loses its anchor when the selection is not in the candidate list
decomp_evidence: CPlayerSystem::OnAction (acclient.c:399731-399747): 0x10000035 = SelectNext(1,1,MONSTER) (closest). 0x10000036 = SelectNext(1,0) then, if unchanged, SelectNext(0,1). 0x10000037 = SelectNext(0,0) then, if unchanged, SelectNext(1,1). OpenAC's retail action table names 0x36 Previous and 0x37 Next, and the same Closest/Previous/Next order holds for compass items (0x2F-0x31), items (0x32-0x34) and players (0x39-0x3B). Inside CPlayerSystem::SelectNext (397944): closer=1 with an anchor keeps the largest distance that is not farther than distToBeat, i.e. one step inward. closer=0 keeps the smallest distance strictly farther, i.e. one step outward (Farther, 395865). So retail Next steps outward and wraps to the nearest; Previous steps inward and wraps to the farthest. The anchor is any selected object that is in a cell (398012 `!_extreme && v9 && v9[12].vfptr` reads `cell` at offset 144), with its own distance as distToBeat (398020); the object does not have to match the selection type. When nothing is selected the anchor falls back to prevSelectedID (398004 `if (selectedID == Formatted /*0*/) oldObjID = prevSelectedID`). With no anchor, closer is flipped (398029), so an unanchored Next picks the farthest and an unanchored Previous picks the nearest. ACCWeenieObject::Remove (438580) sets prevSelectedID to the removed object.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.UI.Abstractions/Input/RetailActionIdentityTable.cs:277-279 (`M(0x10000007, 0x10000036, SelectionPreviousMonster)`, `0x10000037 -> SelectionNextMonster`). src/AcDream.App/Interaction/WorldSelectionQuery.cs:397-413: Next returns the first candidate whose key is greater than the anchor and wraps to `candidates[0]` (nearest); Previous returns the last smaller one and wraps to `candidates[^1]`. SelectionInteractionController.cs:272 uses `anchor = SelectedObjectId ?? PreviousObjectId`. OpenAC differs from the decomp in one place: an unanchored Next returns the nearest (WorldSelectionQuery.cs:390-394).
holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js:8311-8313: `// "next" — NextMonster (1, 0); if unchanged → wrap (0, 1) = farthest.` then `let g = this.selectNext(true, false, type); if (!g) g = this.selectNext(false, true, type);`. discrepancy: Tab ("Next Monster") does what retail Previous Monster does: it steps toward the player and, at the nearest mob, wraps to the farthest. That is exactly the round-4c complaint ('NextMonster from the near drudge jumps to the far stray'). In retail, Next steps outward and wraps to the nearest. Also, when the selection is an NPC, the player themself, or a mob outside the filter, holtburger jumps to the extreme instead of stepping relative to that object's distance. proposed_change: 1. entities.js cycleTarget: swap the two branches. "next" becomes selectNext(false,false) with wrap selectNext(true,true); "previous" becomes selectNext(true,false) with wrap selectNext(false,true). Fix the comments at 8306/8311 and target_cycle.js:205/217. 2. target_cycle.js computeSelectNext: replace `currentGuid` with `anchor` ({guid, dist} or null). distToBeat = anchor.dist even when the anchor guid is not in `list`; still skip candidate === anchor.guid unless extreme (398159). 3. entities.js: add `this._prevSelectedGuid`. Set it in setSelectedTarget when the guid changes and in the despawn clear at 11850 (prev = g, as in ACCWeenieObject::Remove). In selectNext, anchorGuid = `_selectedGuid || _prevSelectedGuid`; use its inst (must exist, not `_attachedParentGuid`, and have root.position) to compute dist with weightedDistance; otherwise anchor = null. 4. index.html `__selectNextTarget` defaults to "next", which will now pick the farthest mob when nothing is selected (retail behaviour). Harness drivers already use "closest"; update the comment at index.html:3362-3370. Optional: the default keys could follow retail (OpenAC uses ' / L / ;), but Tab/Shift+Tab/T is a local choice and not a parity issue.
test_plan: Update `node tests/target_cycle.test.cjs`. The cycle emulator (lines 61-70) uses the swapped dispatch. Sequences become Next = [0xC, 0xA, 0xB, 0xC, 0xA, 0xB] and Previous = [0xA, 0xC, 0xB, 0xA, 0xC, 0xB]. In r4c, Next from the drudge goes to the chicken (one step outward), not the slinker. title: No retail auto-target: after a kill, on entering melee/missile mode, or when attacked with nothing selected, the client never picks the next target
decomp_evidence: ClientCombatSystem::RecvNotice_SelectionChanged (acclient.c:408741): when selectedID == 0 and targetWillinglyLost is not set, and the combat mode is Melee(2) or Missile(4) with PlayerModule::AutoTarget on, it calls ClientCombatSystem::AutoTarget. In melee or missile mode the compass filter (398090-398106) requires ObjectIsAttackable, not a fellow, not a vendor (bitfield 0x200), not REPORT_COLLISIONS_AS_ENVIRONMENT (0x200000), and shown on radar. title: Selection is never dropped when the target is beyond radar range and off-screen
decomp_evidence: CPlayerSystem::RecvNotice_SetSelectedItem (acclient.c:398637): for a newly selected object not owned by the player, the ground container, a vendor or a trade partner, it registers a range handler with RegisterObjectRangeHandler(..., _selectedID, is_player_outside ? 75.0 : 25.0, useRadii=1, ignoreZDelta=1, interval=1.0, 0.0) (398689-398696). CPlayerSystem::CalculateObjectRangeChecks (397612): once a second it calls ACCWeenieObject::ObjectsInRange; with _xy_only set (436730) that is Position::xy_distance <= range. On failure it calls OnObjectRangeExit. CPlayerSystem::OnObjectRangeExit (398710-398737): if `SmartBox::is_selected_object_in_view()` it re-registers; otherwise `ACCWeenieObject::SetSelectedObject(0, 0)`. selected_object_in_view is set only when the selected object's part was actually drawn this frame (CPhysicsPart draw, 314625-314631). The clear goes through SelectionChanged and can then auto-target (selection-2).
openac_evidence: OpenAC does not implement this. RuntimeSelectionEntityFollower.cs:40-71 clears only on Deleted/Withdrawn/Hidden; there is no range or in-view check. The decomp is the only reference.
holt_evidence: The selection is cleared only by despawn (scene3d/entities.js:11850 `if ((this._selectedGuid >>> 0) === g && g !== 0) { this._selectedGuid = 0; ...`) or by picking something else. No code checks range (rg 'RangeExit|out.of.range' in entities.js finds nothing selection-related). Each entity's drawn-this-frame state is available as `inst.root.visible`, the combination of `_stateVisible` and the frustum/distance/occlusion `_renderCullHidden` cull (entities.js:2579-2585, tickEntityRenderVisibility at 2693).
discrepancy: In retail, a target you run away from, or that flees, is dropped once it is more than 75 m (25 m indoors) away in the XY plane and not drawn on screen; the combat UI then auto-targets something nearby. holtburger keeps the stale far target until the server despawns it, so attacks and casts still go to it and auto-target never runs.
proposed_change: Add a pure `selectionRangeExit({xyDist, range, inView, ownedByPlayer})` in target_cycle.js that returns true when !ownedByPlayer && xyDist > range && !inView. In EntityManager.tick, throttle to 1000 ms (retail interval) and evaluate the current `_selectedGuid`. Skip 0, self, `_attachedParentGuid != null`, and items whose Container/Wielder IID (sh.objectInstanceIdProperty(guid, 2/3)) is the player. xyDist = hypot(root.x - pose.x, root.y - pose.y) using `_localPlayerWorldPose()`; range = radarRangeForCell(sh.getCurrentCellId()); inView = inst.root.visible === true. If it returns true, call `_commitSelection(0)` without the willingly-lost flag, so selection-2's auto-target can follow.
test_plan: Add to `node tests/target_cycle.test.cjs`: selectionRangeExit at 80 m outdoors, not in view gives true; same but in view gives false; 74 m gives false; 26 m indoors gives true; owned by player gives false. Add a static assert that entities.js tick calls the helper on a 1000 ms cadence and clears via _commitSelection(0).

title: Click picking tests polygons only; retail falls back to the nearest bounding-sphere hit
decomp_evidence: Render::GfxObjUnderSelectionRay (acclient.c:~380005-380070) runs for every drawn part whose physobj has a server id (check_curr_object, set at 314614). It intersects the ray with the part's drawing_sphere (`CSphere::sphere_intersects_ray`, 380036) and records the nearest sphere hit (dword_86B1B8). With poly-accurate picking it then walks the part's polygons (`CPolygon::polygon_hits_ray`, 380052) and records the nearest polygon hit. Render::GetMouseSelectionObjectID (380089) returns the polygon hit's object if any polygon was hit, otherwise the nearest sphere hit's object. A ray that starts inside a sphere does not count as a sphere hit.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Selection/RetailWorldPicker.cs:18-59: a closestSphere and a closestPolygon per part, `return closestPolygon ?? closestSphere;`. TryIntersectSphere (62-87) rejects `c <= 0` (ray origin inside). Pinned by tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Selection/RetailWorldPickerTests.cs: PolygonHitGloballyBeatsNearerSphereFallback, SphereIsUsedOnlyWhenNoVisiblePolygonHits, DrawingSphereRejectsRayWhichBeginsInsideLikeRetail.
holt_evidence: scene3d/picking.js:911-922: `const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(roots, true); for (const hit of hits) { ... if (obj) return guidByRoot.get(obj); } return null;`. These are triangle hits only, so a miss returns null even when the cursor is a pixel away from a thin weapon, a small ground item or a skinny creature. pickEntityAt is also used for drag-drop give (picking.js:1275) and use-target.
discrepancy: In retail, a click that misses every polygon but falls inside an object's drawing sphere still selects that object (the nearest such sphere). holtburger needs a pixel-exact triangle hit, so small or thin objects are much harder to click than in retail.
proposed_change: In pickEntityAt, after the polygon loop returns nothing, run a sphere pass. For each root in guidByRoot (visible, non-local), call `root.traverseVisible(m => …)` on each Mesh. Ensure `m.geometry.boundingSphere` exists (computeBoundingSphere when it is null; three caches it), copy it to a scratch Sphere, applyMatrix4(m.matrixWorld), skip it if `sphere.containsPoint(raycaster.ray.origin)` (retail rejects an origin inside the sphere), and take `raycaster.ray.intersectSphere(sphere, tmp)`. Keep the nearest t and return that guid. Put the comparison logic in a pure helper (e.g. `pickNearestSphereHit(origin, dir, spheres)` in a new import-free scene3d/pick_math.js) so it can be unit-tested. This approximates retail's per-GfxObj drawing_sphere with three's vertex-derived bounding sphere; a later improvement could expose the DAT drawing_sphere.
test_plan: New `node tests/pick_math.test.mjs` porting the OpenAC RetailWorldPickerTests cases above to plain {center, radius} spheres: the nearest sphere wins when there is no polygon hit; an origin inside a sphere is rejected; a ray that misses gives null; a tie goes to the smaller t. Plus a static assert that picking.js calls the sphere fallback only after the polygon loop finds nothing.

It tests `CSphere::sphere_intersects_ray(mesh->drawing_sphere, ...)`, gated by `!bFoundPolygon || sphereDepth <= nearestPolygonDepth`, and records the nearest sphere hit (byte_86B1A8/dbl_86B1B0/dword_86B1B8). Then, if check_curr_object_polys, it takes the first polygon_hits_ray polygon of the part and keeps the nearest polygon overall. GetMouseSelectionObjectID (380089) returns the polygon object if bFoundPolygon, otherwise the sphere object. find_object calls set_selection_cursor(x,y,1), so picking is poly-accurate (379095-379101). CSphere::sphere_intersects_ray returns 0 when `v5 = |o-c|^2 - r^2 <= 0` (origin inside). OpenAC RetailWorldPicker.cs:18-59 ends with `return closestPolygon ?? closestSphere;`, and TryIntersectSphere rejects `c <= 0`. In holtburger, picking.js:911-922 walks only `raycaster.intersectObjects(roots, true)` triangle hits and returns null on a miss. pickEntityAt is also used by drag-drop give (1276), use-target (950), hover-tooltip.js:224 (mousemove), debug-overlay.js:269 (rAF), item_drag.js:516 and camera.js:860.

When walking meshes, resolve each mesh's owner by climbing to the nearest root in guidByRoot (the same walk as the polygon path), not to the outer entity. (b) Restrict the fallback to rig-part meshes: Mesh children under inst.parts, visible, and not hidden by materialRendersNothing (entities.js:4713). (b - sqrt(disc))/a : (b + sqrt(disc))/a (retail/OpenAC form). Skip t < 0, which is behind the camera (retail never draws those). Keep the minimum t, ties by first seen. The owner guid comes from climbing parents to the nearest guidByRoot key. Feed the result to pickNearestSphereHit with raycaster.ray.origin/direction. 3. title: Attacking with a monster's held weapon selected is refused instead of attacking the monster, and the empty-selection message is not retail's
decomp_evidence: ClientCombatSystem::GetAttackTarget (acclient.c:407570): returns 0 if nothing is selected or the selected weenie IsOwnedByPlayer. Otherwise `v3 = GetPhysicsObject(selected); v4 = v3[5].hash_next; if (v4) v1 = v4->id;`, where HashBaseData is {vfptr@0, hash_next@4, id@8}, so element 5's hash_next is offset 64, which is CPhysicsObj::parent in the PDB dump. So selecting a wielded item attacks its wielder. ClientCombatSystem::ExecuteAttack (408626-408660): when there is no valid target, with or without a selection, it prints `"You must select a valid combat target before attacking"`.
openac_evidence: OpenAC does not port the parent redirection. Its explicit-selection rule is RuntimeAttackTargetResolver.cs:55-65 with IsAttackableSelection; its refusal is the enum only (RuntimeAttackTargetRefusal NothingSelected/SelectionNotAttackable). The decomp is the reference here.
holt_evidence: scene3d/picking.js:1323-1334: `const targetGuid = getSelectedTarget(); if (targetGuid === 0) { ... emitActionRejected("Select a target first."); return; } if (!entityIsAttackableTarget(targetGuid)) { emitActionRejected("You must select a valid combat target before attacking"); ...`. If `entityMap.get(sel)?._attachedParentGuid` is set, return that parent guid; otherwise return sel. Use it at the top of fireAttackOnSelectedTarget and in the follow-up path, then run entityIsAttackableTarget on the result. Replace "Select a target first." with retail's "You must select a valid combat target before attacking" for both cases. title: Formula-untargeted spells (war rings/walls/sprays) demand a selected target; wasm isUntargeted mis-ports CSpellBase::IsUntargeted
decomp_evidence: ClientMagicSystem::CastSpell (acclient.c:404732-404754) checks `if (spellBase._bitfield & 8)` first and casts self-targeted spells at the player through FreeHandsAndCastSpell. Otherwise `if (!CSpellBase::InqTargetType(&spellBase)) { cmdinterp->vfptr[16](); CM_Magic::Event_CastUntargetedSpell(_spellID); IncrementBusyCount }`, with no selection required. CSpellBase::InqTargetType (acclient.c:449055) is `InqSpellFormula; result = SpellFormula::Complete(&formula); if (result) result = SpellFormula::GetTargetingType(&formula);`. CSpellBase::IsUntargeted (acclient.c:449226) is `return SpellFormula::GetTargetingType(&result) == 0;`. GetTargetingType (487766) takes the last non-zero component from slot 4 onward; GetTargetTypeFromComponentID (487059) maps 0x31-0x38, 0x3C-0x3E and 0xBE to 0x10, 0x39 to 560015 (0x88B8F), 0x3B to 268500992 (0x10010000), and everything else to 0. The cast button (gmSpellcastingUI::UpdateCastButtonTooltip, acclient.c:248523) enables without a selection when `CSpellBase::IsUntargeted || _bitfield & 8`.
openac_evidence: RetailSpellFormula.cs:36-56 implements GetTargetingType and GetTargetTypeFromComponentId. RetailSpellMetadataProjector.cs:25 computes `formulaTargetType = RetailSpellFormula.GetTargetingType(formula)`, and :49 sets IsUntargeted = `formulaTargetType == 0u`. RuntimeSpellCastState.cs:101-105 sends untargeted with no selection. Tests: RetailSpellFormulaTests.cs:19-46 (TargetComponent_UsesRetailItemTypeMask, TargetingType_MapsFinalPopulatedFormulaComponent).
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/spell_table.rs:220-225 has the doc comment 'Mirrors CSpellBase::IsUntargeted' but implements `self.non_component_target_type == 0`, which reads the wrong field; crates/holtburger-world/src/spell.rs:115-117 does the same, and src/lib.rs:35336 exports it as isUntargeted. Cast routing ignores it anyway. plugins/spellbook.js:146 sets `untargeted:  !!raw.isSelfTargeted,`, and the LSD fallback catalog's _comment says 'untargeted is derived from SpellFlags.SelfTargeted (0x8)'. combat-bar.js:1271/1302/859 use `(meta?.untargeted ?? true)` and then either toast 'select a target first' (1278-1288) or arm the spell (1314). hotbar.js:136-147 spellIsSelfTargeted feeds decideFireAction (168-181), which returns needTarget. Applying retail InqTargetType to the DAT-decrypted formulas in data/spell-table-attrs.json gives 272 of 6266 spells with target type 0 and no SelfTargeted bit: 256 War, 13 Life, 3 Void. title: Cast busy is a per-spell time estimate, not retail's outstanding-request counter: a different-spell recast preempts the live local cast while ACE answers YoureTooBusy
decomp_evidence: ClientMagicSystem::CastSpell and FreeHandsAndCastSpell (acclient.c:403775-403792, 404751-404752) never test busy: they always send, then call ClientUISystem::IncrementBusyCount. IncrementBusyCount (acclient.c:401885) is `m_cBusy + 1` and only updates the cursor state. ClientUISystem::Handle_Item__UseDone (acclient.c:401924-401937) does `m_cBusy--` on every UseDone, error or not. Busy is a count of outstanding requests, cleared only by UseDone.
openac_evidence: RuntimeSpellCastState.cs:135-154: StopCompletely, then send, then IncrementBusy, then `_outstandingCastReceipts++`. CompleteUse (168-203) decrements once per receipt. Test Cast_ReissuesWhileAReceiptIsPending (RuntimeSpellCastStateTests.cs:146-162) covers two sends, two receipts and a pending spell held until the last receipt.
holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js:8748-8749: `const sameSpell = !CAST_BUSY_SCOPE || (inst._castBusySpellId === (spellId >>> 0)); if (sameSpell && inst._castBusyUntilMs && nowMs < inst._castBusyUntilMs) return;`. CAST_BUSY_SCOPE defaults on (entities.js:1506-1514), with the rationale 'a different-spell weave the server will accept still animates locally'. Vanilla ACE does not accept it: PropertyManager.cs:597 `spellcast_recoil_queue` defaults false, so a recast while IsBusy gets UseDone(YoureTooBusy) (Player_Magic.cs:117-125, VerifyBusy 376-383), as WS08-cast-lifecycle.md (D) itself notes. The new chain bumps the token and cuts off chain A. cast_reject_policy.js:45-46 excludes 0x001D from cancellation, so the phantom chain B is never cut. `_castBusyUntilMs` is also zeroed when the chain ends naturally (entities.js:9081-9083), before ACE's FinishCast recoil and UseDone, so same-spell spam inside that window also starts a phantom chain.

decomp_evidence: ClientMagicSystem::CastSpell (acclient.c:404698-404719): `if (AreSpellComponentsRequired() && (GetAppropriateSpellFormula(&formula, &spellBase), ..., GetNumSpellComponents > 0))`, then for each component `SpellComponentTable::SCIDtoWCID` + `ComponentTracker::ComponentIsOwned(tracker, wcid)`; a miss prints "You do not have all of this spell's components". AreSpellComponentsRequired (404438-404467) is PlayerDesc `InqBool(0x44, &required)` with default 1. GetAppropriateSpellFormula (404515-404605): an infusion int (297/296/295/294/328) above 0, or `MagicPackIsOwned(SchoolOfMagic2WCID)`, selects InqScarabOnlyFormula; otherwise `InqCustomizedSpellFormula(account_name)`. SCIDtoWCID (487319) is an EnumIDMap lookup. SpellExamineUI::ExamineSpell (234697) also displays GetAppropriateSpellFormula.
openac_evidence: SpellComponentRequirementService.cs:41-107: the bool 68 bypass, WCID ownership through the containment chain, infusion or magic pack selecting the scarab-only formula, otherwise CustomizeForAccount. RetailSpellFormula.cs:59-188: InqScarabOnlyFormula, ComputeNameHash, RandomizeVersion1/2/3, which rewrite only taper slots (63 + n%12). MagicCatalog.cs:113-130 builds SCID->WCID from DualEnumIDMap 0x27000002. Tests in SpellComponentRequirementServiceTests.cs: ServerDisabledComponents_BypassesPreflightAndUsesModernFormula, PersonalizedFormula_UsesExactCanonicalAccountSpelling, InfusedSchoolOrDirectlyCarriedFocus_UsesScarabOnlyFormula.
holt_evidence: ui/ac_cast_precheck.js:34-39 defaults to 'off'. :153 `const compIds = _recField(rec, "components")` reads the base decrypted formula, not the account-customized one. :63-79 matches by name substring (:76 `it === name || it.includes(name) || name.includes(it)`) instead of by WCID. There is no bool 68 check and no foci or infusion handling. plugins/spellbook.js:610-614 renders `Components: ${names}` from the same base formula. ACE consumes the personalized formula: Player_Magic.cs:1227-1246 HasComponentsForSpell -> spell.Formula.GetPlayerFormula(this), and ~/ace-server ACE.DatLoader/FileTypes/SpellTable.cs:58-69 GetSpellFormula(..., accountName) -> RandomizeVersion1/2/3. ACE sends SpellComponentsRequired=false when require_spell_comps is off (Player_Networking.cs:232-235). holtburger-dat already parses DualDidMapper 0x27 (file_type/dual_did_mapper.rs), and SessionHandle exposes accountName.
discrepancy: Retail always checked components client-side, against the formula the server actually consumes, by WCID. Holtburger's opt-in check falsely refuses in three cases: a player holding their personalized tapers, a server with components disabled, and a player carrying a focus or infusion augmentation. Its spellbook shows base-formula tapers that ACE will not accept, so the UI can tell players to carry the wrong tapers.
